OVERVIEW
We primarily manufacture and sell robotic products, and, to a lesser extent, provide related robotic
solutionsinChineseMainlandandoverseasmarkets,dedicatedtothedesign,development,manufacturing
and commercialization of our offerings. Leveraging our proprietary technology platform, we have
cultivated a dynamic robotic application portfolio, comprising industrial robots, flexible collaborative
robots, embodied intelligent robots, and related robotic solutions characterized by performance, agility,
intelligence, safety and robustness.
We provide a broad portfolio of intelligent robots and robotic solutions. Our industrial robots are
engineered for manufacturing applications requiring significant speed, precision, and operational
reliability. For processes necessitating seamless human-robot collaboration, our collaborative robots
enable flexible manufacturing and intricate operations such as precision assembly and welding. Our
embodied intelligent robots are the industry’s first to achieve large-scale commercial deployment in the
consumerelectronicssector,accordingtotheCICReport,performingtasksincludingassemblyoperations,
material handling and unmanned retail. Leveraging our broad product portfolio, proprietary technology
platform, and expansive service network, we deliver robots and robotic solutions to over 1,000 customers
from diverse industry sectors across over 40 countries and regions.
We are one of the earliest domestic companies in China capable of producing both industrial and
collaborative robots at an annual production exceeding 1,000 units, reflecting an industry trend toward
integrated manufacturing automation, according to the CIC Report. Although our business scale is
relatively modest, this early capability was enabled by our proprietary robot technology platform and
strategicR&Dfocusonconcurrentdevelopmentofbothproductlinesfromtheoutset.Intermsofrevenue
in2025,werankedNo.6amongdomesticrobotprovidersinChina’sindustrialrobotmarketwithamarket
share of 0.9%, and No. 6 in China’s collaborative robot market with a market share of 4.8%, according
to the CIC Report. We are also the only provider of flexible collaborative robots at an annual production
exceeding 1,000 units among the top six collaborative robot providers in China. We are also one of the
top five providers in China’s embodied intelligent robotic arm market with a market share of 6.3%,
according to the same source.
Our Market Opportunity
Driven by the accelerating population aging, rising labor costs, expanding downstream application
scenarios, and growing policy support, China’s industrial robot industry has continued to grow and is
expected to reach RMB37.3 billion in 2030, at a CAGR of 9.3% from 2025 to 2030, according to the CIC
Report. Within this industry, China’s vertical articulated robot market is expected to reach RMB29.9

Collaborative robots are agile, safe, and easy-to-use machines that drive growth in intelligent
automation. They enable seamless human-machine collaboration on production lines and fill application
gaps beyond traditional industrial robots. Flexible collaborative robots have emerged to achieve built-in
high-precision torque sensors in every joint, enabling refined force control and enhanced performance in
accuracy,safety,andadaptability.China’sflexiblecollaborativerobotmarketisexpectedtoreachRMB4.6
billion in 2030, at a CAGR of 32.4% from 2025 to 2030, according to the CIC Report. In 2025, we ranked
No. 6 in China’s collaborative robot market by sales revenue with a market share of 4.8%, and we are the
only scaled provider of flexible collaborative robot products among the top six manufacturers, according
to the same source.

force control precision, on par with top international competitors.This enables efficient and rapid product

SUMMARY
Our technology platform is built on a suite of proprietary core technologies. The foundation of our
platform is our proprietary robot design technology, powered by our self-designed xCore control system.
This system supports multiple robot types and is enhanced by our embodied AI model training platform,
which adds advanced AI capabilities in terms of multimodal perception, adaptive decision-making and
real-time motion control to our robotic offerings. Our xCore control system offers standardized interfaces
for hardware and process package expansion, allowing customers and partners to deploy customized
solutionsontheirownwhilebenefitingfromsharedAIinsightsthataddresslast-milechallengesinvarious
application scenarios. We provide full technical support through, among others, documentation,
communityforums,andtrainingprograms.OurAIServiceAgentenablespredictivemaintenancetoreduce
downtime and ensure continuous operation. Based on our technology stack, we offer a diverse range of
robots and process packages for a wide variety of application scenarios.
OUR ROBOTICS OFFERINGS
Our robotics offerings comprise a combination of robots and robotic solutions, which are marketed
under multiple series and are well-suited for tasks in industrial, commercial services and healthcare
scenarios. We offer our robots under three principal categories based on their application scenarios and
interaction capabilities. Designed to meet diverse application scenarios ranging from high-speed,
high-precision manufacturing to safe and flexible human-robot interaction, our robots comprise industrial
robots, flexible collaborative robots, and embodied intelligent robots. We also provide industry-tailored
robotic solutions, enabling intelligent automation across diverse industrial scenarios. Our robots are
standardized products that come with multiple standard options tailored to common application scenarios.

Our Robots
Industrial Robots
Industrial robots are programmable robotic arms with multiple degrees of freedom, designed for
autonomous positioning and control. Equipped with joints and sensors, they can perceive their
environment,makedecisions,andperformphysicaltasksandareidealforreplacingmanuallaborinharsh,
– 2 –

SUMMARY
repetitive, or hazardous conditions. We offer a broad portfolio of industrial robots deployed across a wide
range of application scenarios, including primarily the manufacturing scenarios. Our product line is
segmented based on payload capacity into three categories, i.e., light-payload, medium-payload and
heavy-payload, each engineered to meet the specific performance requirements of distinct industrial
applications. The following diagram sets forth an illustration of our industrial robot series.
Flexible Collaborative Robots
Collaborative robots are a key growth driver in intelligent automation, designed for safe, seamless
human-robot collaboration. Unlike traditional industrial robots, they feature lightweight structures,
adaptive motion, and enhanced safety mechanisms, allowing them to operate alongside workers without
physical barriers. In particular, our collaborative robots consist entirely of flexible collaborative robots,
asopposedtotraditionalcollaborativerobots.Specifically,ourflexiblecollaborativerobotshaveachieved
built-in high-precision torque sensors in every joint, leveraging our integrated joint force control
technology, which enables refined force control and enhanced performance in accuracy, safety, and
adaptability. We deploy our flexible collaborative robots primarily in the manufacturing and commercial
services scenarios. The following diagram sets forth an illustration of our flexible collaborative robot
series.

Embodied Intelligent Robots

embodied intelligent robot companies in terms of market valuation are using or have already switched to
our humanoid arms for product iteration. We continue to enhance our robot body design and develop

Our Robotic Solutions
We provide industry-tailored solutions to address unique operational needs of our customers. Our
robotic solutions typically embody one or more robots we offer. We work closely with customers to
develop one-stop solutions that address specific challenges and enhance operational efficiency. By
customizing robotic solutions in new industry sectors on a project-based basis to set benchmark projects,
we standardize our solutions and attract new customers in new sectors to scale our business. Our
benchmarkprojectsprovidingstandardizedsolutionsinspecificindustriestoleadingcustomershavebuilt
a broad and high-quality customer base in those industry sectors, providing a solid foundation for
sustained growth. See “Business—Our Robotics Offerings” for details.
COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS
We believe the following competitive strengths have contributed to our success and differentiated us
from our competitors: (1) we have built a robotic technology platform through forward design and
development, (2) product coverage across three robot categories supported by rapid and cost-effective
business deployment capability, (3) established customer and partnership network backed by our service
capabilityandmodularplug-insandopeninterfaces,and(4)experiencedseniormanagementandbusiness

PATH TO PROFITABILITY
During the Track Record Period, while our revenue grew rapidly, our overall revenue scale was still
insufficient to fully absorb our largely fixed cost base, resulting in limited operating leverage. Our
business model focuses on long-term value creation through sustained investment in core technology
platforms,includinginternallydevelopedsoftwarealgorithms.Inparallel,weinvestedheavilyinbuilding
an increasingly larger sales and marketing team to support business expansion and customer acquisition.
Goingforward,weintendtocontinuetogrowourrevenue,improveournetprofitmarginandimprovenet
operatingcashoutflowpositiontodriveupprofitability.Fordetails,see“Business—PathtoProfitability.”
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
We have built a platform that fully integrates technology, products and applications. The foundation
of our platform is our proprietary robot design technology, powered by our self-designed xCore control

enhancement of the core technologies for robotics, which we have established significant expertise since

We have continued to expand our network of partners and customers subsequent to theTrack Record
Period.Inparticular,thesalesvolumeofourroboticproductshasbeenonanupwardtrajectory.Inthefirst
quarter of 2026, we introduced and began mass production of our HSA series force-controlled joint
modules for humanoid robots. We also achieved a total shipment volume of over 5,100 robotic products
in the first quarter of 2026, including over 2,000 embodied intelligent robots. As of March 31, 2026, we
had confirmed orders in process of RMB577.3 million, including RMB510.2 million of robotic product
orders and RMB66.3 million of robotic solution orders. In 2026, we expect to record increasing net loss,
primarily as a result of (1) the share-based compensation expenses recognized prior to the Listing, as the
vesting condition of the shares awarded is contingent on the Listing, and therefore no share-based
compensation expenses is recognized until the Listing is concluded highly probable in 2026; and (2) the
further accrual of interest expense on redemption liabilities in connection with our Pre-IPO Investments,
which is expected to adversely affect our financial performance in 2026. Upon Listing, the redemption
rightswillbeterminatedandtherelatedredemptionliabilitieswillbederecognised,andwewillnolonger
recognise such interest expense thereafter.

audited consolidated financial information of our Group was prepared) and there is no event since

INTERNATIONAL TRADE POLICIES, GEOPOLITICS, AND TRADE RESTRICTIONS
We are subject to risks from the continuously evolving international trade and regulatory
environment, including in areas such as export controls, sanctions, and foreign investments. These
dynamics can adversely affect our supply chain, limit our access to markets or technologies, and increase
our compliance costs and operational complexity.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, our procurement and sales
have complied with the U.S. export control laws and regulations. Although we conducted Russia-related
business, we are advised by our International Sanctions LegalAdvisor that (1) our sales to Russia did not
constitute primary sanctioned activity as defined under Chapter 4.4 of the Guide for New Listing
Applicants (the “Primary Sanctioned Activity”) and the exposure to secondary sanctions risks is remote
under the U.S. sanction laws; (2) for other jurisdictions, our business complies with the applicable
sanctions laws and regulations of the jurisdictions where we operate. Apart from the aforesaid, we have
not engaged in sanctioned or sanctionable activity involving any person listed on the sanctions lists of the
UnitedNations(“U.N.”),theEuropeanUnion(“E.U.”),theUnitedKingdom(“U.K.”),Australia,andother
applicable jurisdictions. Although the relevant jurisdictions impose sanctions against Russia, given that
our Russian-related businesses have no nexus with the E.U., U.K., Australia and other applicable
jurisdiction, our International Sanctions LegalAdvisor is of the view that there are no indications that our
business have violated applicable sanctions laws and regulations in all jurisdictions where we operated
during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.
Apart from our Russia-related business, one of our customers was listed on the SDNs List (the
“SDNs Customer”) in September 2024. We conducted transactions with the SDNs Customer in December
2024,July2025,andOctober2025afteritsdesignationontheSDNsListtherevenuegeneratedfromsuch
SDNsCustomeraccountedfor0.1%and0.01%oftheGroup’stotalrevenuefor2024and2025.Asadvised
by our International Sanctions LegalAdvisor, in the absence of evidence indicating that our business with
theSDNsCustomermayinvolvedeceptivepracticesusedtoevadeU.S.sanctions,sincenoU.S.nexuswas
involved in the transactions with the SDNs Customer, such transactions do not constitute Primary
Sanctioned Activities. We ceased all transactions with the SDNs Customer in October 2025.
Inaddition,onOctober28,2024,theU.S.DepartmentoftheTreasuryissuedaOutboundInvestment
Rule on outbound investment, or the Outbound Investment Rule, to implement an outbound investment
program that restricts investments by U.S. persons and U.S.-controlled entities imposed by Executive
Order 14105, “Addressing United States Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and
Products in Countries of Concern.” The Outbound Investment Rule became effective on January 2, 2025.
Under the Outbound Investment Rule, we are advised by our International Sanctions Legal Advisor that
our business should be categorized as a notifiable activity, as we have developed an AI system intended
to be used for the control of robotics systems. Therefore, we are advised by our International Sanctions
Legal Advisor that we are a “covered foreign person” under the Outbound Investment Rule, and U.S.
person’s investment to us constitutes a notifiable transaction. However, once our H Shares are issued and
become publicly traded, subsequent purchasers are exempted under the publicly traded securities
exception. See “Business—Trade Restrictions, Sanctions, and Tariff” and “Risk Factors—Risks Relating
to Our General Operations and Industry—We are exposed to risks associated with U.S. Executive Order
14105 and its implementing regulations that prohibit and require notification by U.S. persons for certain
investments.”

GLOSSARY
This glossary contains certain technical terms used in this prospectus in connection with our
Companyandourbusiness.Suchtermsandtheirmeaningsmaynotcorrespondtostandardindustry
definitions or usage.
“absolute positioning accuracy” the precision with which a robot can move to a specific point in its
workspace relative to a fixed coordinate system
“AC servo motors” a servo control system powered by alternating current (AC) that
precisely controls the position, speed, and torque of an electric
motor, which is widely used in industrial robots, CNC machine
tools, automation equipment, and other fields
“algorithm” a step-by-step procedure or set of rules, often implemented in
computer code, designed to perform a specific task or solve a
particular problem
“artificial intelligence” or “AI” the ability of a machine or computer system to perform tasks that
typically require human intelligence
“automation” the application of various control systems, such as controller,
robots, and information technologies, to operate equipment and
processes in a wide range of industries
“axis” or “axes” a degree of freedom, where increasing the number of axes allows
the cobot to access a greater amount of space by giving it more
degrees of freedom
“CAGR” compound annual growth rate
“collaborative robots” robots with operational robotic arms intended for direct human-
robot interaction or collaboration within a shared space or where
humans and robots are operating in proximity
“controllers” systems connected to the robot in order to control the movements
of the robots

GLOSSARY
“embodied intelligent robots” a new generation of robotic systems built on the core concept of
embodied intelligence, functioning as intelligent agents that rely
on a physical body to perceive, interact, and act within their
environment
“encoders” electromechanical devices designed to convert mechanical motion
into electrical signals, which can provide feedback on angular
velocity and displacement
“end-effector” the tool mounted on the robot according to the customer’s
requirements, such as vacuum suction cups, pneumatic grippers,
electric grippers, specialized jigs, or dispensing valves
“flexible collaborative robots” robotic systems with native force control capabilities, featuring
built-in high-precision torque sensors in each joint that enable
global multi-point force control
“force sensor” a sensor that measures force by converting the input of mechanical
force into the output of an electrical signal
“full-state feedback” an advanced perception and response mechanism within a robotic
control system, referring to a robot’s ability to acquire and process
complete state information of all its joints and end effectors in real
time during operation
“GB 9706” a series of mandatory standards for medical electrical equipment,
requiredbytheNationalMedicalProductsAdministration(NMPA)
in China
“IEC 60601” a series of international standards, published by the International
Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), that specify safety and
performance requirements for medical electrical equipment and is
widely recognized as the benchmark for medical device safety
“industrial robots” automatically controlled, reprogrammable, multi-purpose robotic
arms used for automation applications in industrial environments
“IP67” ingress protection rating, with 6 referring to the highest level of
protection for solids to withstand solid foreign objects on a scale
of 0 to 6, and 7 referring to water protection rating against the
effects of immersion in water for 30 minutes and one meter deep
“ISO” International Organization for Standardization, an independent
international organization that develops and publishes
international standards across various industries. These standards
cover a wide range of topics, including quality, safety, efficiency,
and interoperability
“MTBF certification” a certification of the mean time between failures, which measures
the reliability of a product

because(1)ourcustomerstendtoplacetheirordersand/orcompletetheirinspectionsinthethirdorfourth
quartertomaintainbettercontrolovertheirannualcapitalexpenditureandrealizetheirannualbudget,and
(2) our customers tend to schedule their procurement in advance of the major holidays in China and
overseas markets, many of which are in the fourth quarter, to avoid potential shipment disruptions and
other logistic issues caused by holidays at the beginning of a new year. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our
revenue recognized in the second half of the year was RMB192.6 million, RMB208.0 million and
RMB345.9 million, accounting for 72.1%, 64.0% and 66.3% of our total revenue in the same periods,
respectively.AccordingtotheCICReport,suchseasonalityisgenerallyprevalentintheroboticsindustry.
The degree of seasonality may vary from year to year due to conditions in the industry and other
factors, which makes it difficult for us to predict the level of demand with precision. If seasonal demand
exceeds our expectation, we may not have sufficient stock or arrange for timely production and delivery.
If seasonal demand is lower than our expectation, we could be left with excess inventory, higher working
capital and liquidity requirements, as well as the risk of impairment losses on our inventory. Furthermore,
our operating and financial results for an interim period may not be representative of our overall
performance for a year. We expect to continue to experience seasonal fluctuations in our revenue, results
of operations and financial condition.

individuals, or to bring an action against us or against these individuals in the event that you believe your
rights have been infringed under the applicable securities laws or otherwise.
On January 14, 2019, the Supreme People’s Court of the PRC and the government of Hong Kong
Special Administrative Region signed the Arrangement on Reciprocal Recognition and Enforcement of
Judgments in Civil and Commercial Matters by the Courts of the Mainland and of the Hong Kong Special
Administrative Region (關於內地與香港特別行政區法院相互認可和執行民商事案件判決的安排) (the
“2019 Arrangement”), which took effect on January 29, 2024. The 2019 Arrangement seeks to establish
a mechanism with greater clarity and certainty for recognition and enforcement of judgments in a wider
range of civil and commercial matters between Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong, based on criteria other
than a written bilateral choice of court agreement. Under the 2019Arrangement, any party concerned may
apply to the relevant PRC or Hong Kong court for recognition and enforcement of the effective judgments
in civil and commercial cases, subject to the conditions set forth in the 2019 Arrangement. However, we
cannot assure you that all final judgments will be recognized and effectively enforced by the relevant
Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong court.
Thereisnoassurancewhetherandwhenwewillpaydividends,whichissubjecttorestrictionsunder
PRC law.
Under PRC laws, dividends may be paid only out of distributable profits. Distributable profits are
defined as our profits after taxes as determined under applicable accounting standards less any recovery
of accumulated losses and appropriations to statutory and other reserves that we are required to make.As
a result, we may not have sufficient, if any, distributable profits to enable our Company to make dividend
distributions to its shareholders in the future, including periods for which our Company’s financial
statements indicate that our operations have been profitable.Any distributable profits not distributed in a
given year are retained and available for distribution in subsequent years.
Moreover, because the calculation of distributable profits under PRC GAAP is different from the
calculation under the HKFRS in certain respects, our Company may not have distributable profits as
determined under PRC GAAP, even if it has profits for that year as determined under the HKFRS, or vice
versa.Accordingly,wemaynotreceivesufficientdistributionsfromourPRCsubsidiaries.Restrictionson
dividend payment could have a negative impact on our ability to make dividend distributions to our
Shareholders in the future, including those periods in which our financial statements indicate that our
operations have been profitable.

Kong dollars for the purpose of making payments for dividends on our H Shares or for other business
purposes, appreciation of the Hong Kong dollar against Renminbi would have a negative effect on the
Hong Kong dollar amount available to us.

OVERVIEW OF INDUSTRIAL ROBOT INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification of Industrial Robots
As global manufacturing systems are accelerating their transition to automation and intelligence,
industrial robots are emerging as core executive units in smart manufacturing systems. Driven by the
continuous advancement of digital technologies and the constant upgrading of manufacturing models,
industrialrobotsarenolongerconfinedtotheroleoftraditionalautomatedtools.Instead,byvirtueoftheir
intelligentdecision-makingandflexibleresponsecapabilitiesacrossmultiplescenarios,theyhavebecome
key drivers for the transformation of production paradigms in the new wave of industrial transformation.
Meanwhile, driven by factors such as geopolitical frictions, redundant capacity expansion, demographic
changes, imbalance between labor supply and demand, and enterprises’ urgent demand for efficient and
flexible production, there is growing adoption of industrial robots in industry sectors such as
manufacturing, commercial services, and healthcare.
Industrialrobotsrefertoautomaticallycontrolled,reprogrammable,multi-purposeroboticarmsused
for automation applications in industrial environments. Their mechanical structures are similar to human
arms, enabling flexible trajectory planning and complex operational tasks. Different from collaborative
robots, industrial robots are often used in dedicated industrial workplaces, which is restricted by safety
barriers as they are not designed for direct human interactions. Based on robot type, industrial robots can
be mainly further categorized into the following types:
Type Definitions
Vertical Articulated Vertical articulated robots refer to multi-joint robotic arms or multi-degree-
Robots of-freedom robots designed for industrial applications. They typically
feature six degrees of freedom and possess characteristics such as flexible
spatial movement, high load-carrying capacity, and high-precision path
control, enabling them to perform multi-angle operations within complex
industrial processes. In practical applications, such robots generally require
safe operating distances or protective isolation measures to ensure
operational safety.
SCARA Robots SCARA robots are high-speed, high-precision industrial robots featuring a
horizontally articulated multi-joint structure.
Delta Robots Delta robots are lightweight, high-speed robots utilizing a parallel
triangular structure.
Source: IFR, MIR, CIC
Industrial Chain Analysis of the Industrial Robot Market
The upstream of the industrial robot industry mainly consists of providers of core components and
supporting basic components. Core components include controllers, servo motors, and reducers, while
supporting basic components mainly cover sensors, end effectors, etc. The midstream mainly involves
R&D, production, and system integration. The downstream application of the industrial robot industry
covers multiple industrial fields and end-process scenarios, such as automotive and auto parts, 3C
electronics, new energy, general manufacturing, healthcare, and commercial services.

Market Size of Industrial Robot Industry
Globally, the industrial robot market has continued to expand as manufacturers accelerate
automation deployment to enhance production resilience, improve operational efficiency and respond to
evolving supply chain configurations. The global robot market reached RMB93.9 billion in 2025 and is
expected to further increase to RMB160.8 billion by 2030, representing a CAGR of 11.3% from 2025 to
2030.
Drivenbymultiplefactorsincludingtheacceleratingpopulationaging,risinglaborcosts,expanding
downstream application scenarios, and growing policy support, China’s industrial robot market reached
RMB23.9 billion in 2025. During this period, the impact of the pandemic pushed downstream
manufacturing to accelerate automation transformation, leading to the concentrated release of short-term
demand. Coupled with excessive capacity expansion in some industries, a certain degree of structural
overcapacity emerged.At the same time, uneven global macroeconomic recovery and weakening external
demand made manufacturing investment more cautious, resulting in a phased slowdown in market growth
from 2023 to 2024. In the next five years, China’s industrial robot market is expected to reach RMB37.3
billion in 2030, at a CAGR of 9.3% from 2025 to 2030.
In terms of sales volume, China’s industrial robot market increased from 240.7 thousand units in
2021 to 293.9 thousand in 2025, at a CAGR of 5.1%. Among them, vertical articulated robots still
maintained a large scale, at a CAGR of 5.6%. The sales volume of China’s industrial robot market is
expected to reach 465.3 thousand units, at a CAGR of 9.6% from 2025 to 2030.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Drivers of China’s Industrial Robot Industries
 Labor shortage leading to increased labor costs. Global aging and the declining share of
working-age population have made labor shortages more common in major manufacturing countries
includingChina.From2020to2030,theproportionofthepopulationaged65andaboveisexpected
to increase from 9.3% to nearly 12%. In addition, labor costs have continued to rise. Meanwhile, the
average annual wage in the manufacturing industry increased from RMB74.6 thousand in 2020 to
over RMB100 thousand in 2025 and is expected to further increase to approximately RMB130
thousand by 2030, representing a CAGR of 6.0%.As a result, robot manufacturers are increasingly
adopting industrial robots to reduce labor dependence, improve production stability, and control
costs.
 Industrial intelligent transformation driving expansion of downstream application scope. The
manufacturing industry is in a critical period of evolution from “automated production” to
“intelligent manufacturing.” As a result, industrial robots not only undertake repetitive labor tasks
but also gradually extend to processes such as high-precision assembly, complex process machining,
and flexible production scheduling.
 Continuous innovation in core technologies driving down production costs. The localization of key
components such as controllers, servo motors, and reducers is accelerating in China, strengthening
supply chain independence and reducing production costs. Meanwhile, AI technologies are
improving robots’ perception, learning, and collaboration capabilities. With the development of
embodied intelligence, industrial robots are gradually evolving into more adaptive and intelligent
systems, further lowering adoption barriers and supporting market expansion.
 Favorable policy support from governments worldwide. Governments generally regard the robot
industry as an important part of strategic emerging industries and have introduced industrial support
policies and special development plans covering R&D investment, industrial chain improvement,
application demonstrations, and market promotion. In 2024, China issued the Implementation Plan
for Promoting Equipment Upgrades in the Industrial Sector (推動工業領域設備更新實施方案),
whichencouragesthedeploymentofsmartmanufacturingequipmentsuchasindustrialrobotsinkey
production and logistics processes.
Development Trends and Opportunities of China’s Industrial Robot Industries
 Domestic market players are accelerating global expansion. With the advancement of the domestic
substitution, Chinese market players have been continuously enhancing their core technologies,
productperformance,andsystemintegrationcapabilities.Whilesteadilyexpandingtheirshareinthe
domestic market, these market players are actively establishing overseas operations.
 Accelerated evolution of new types of intelligent industrial robots expanding scope of applications.
New types of intelligent industrial robots such as embodied intelligent robots, composite robots, and
dual-arm collaborative robots are constantly maturing and expanding the boundaries of operational
tasks in industrial scenarios. These advanced types possess the capabilities of complex process
operations and precise motion execution, enabling them to penetrate more high-difficulty industrial
segments, such as precision assembly, flexible production, and high-reliability testing.
Threats and Challenges of China’s Industrial Robot Industries
 High Dependence on Core Components. Key components such as reducers, servo motors, and
high-performance controllers still rely partly on imports. Domestic providers require further
advancement in precision control, consistency, and durability performance. Fluctuations in the
supplyandcostofthesecorecomponentsmayaffectdeliveryschedulesandcoststructuresofsystem
integrators and robot providers, thereby creating uncertainties in profitability.
 Rising Demand for System Integration and Customization. Different downstream industries have
varying requirements for flexibility, precision, and stability. Customers are placing greater emphasis
on full-line integration capability and alignment with industry-specific solutions, making it difficult
for single-function mechanical performance to serve as a sustainable competitive advantage.
Companies must continue to invest in software algorithms, machine vision, and system integration
to meet the needs of complex processes and flexible production environments.
Entry Barriers to China’s Industrial Robot Industries
 Core components and motion control capabilities. Industrial robots require high precision, stability
and durability in core components such as controllers, servo systems and reducers. New entrants
need long-term accumulation in motion control, trajectory planning and reliability validation.
 System integration and customer validation. Downstream customers usually require customized
deployment based on specific production lines. Companies need strong process know-how, project
delivery capabilities and after-sales service support, making it difficult for new entrants to gain
customer trust in the short term.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Cost Structure and Trend of China’s Industrial Robot Industry
The major costs of industrial robots are primarily attributed to servo systems and reducers. Servo
systems serve as the power and motion execution units responsible for driving joint movement and
controlling speed, position, and torque, while reducers are transmission components installed at robot
joints to reduce speed and increase output torque. Together, servo systems and reducers accounted for
approximately 60% to 65% of total cost in 2025. In addition, controllers, which function as the core
control units of industrial robots, accounted for approximately 10% of total cost, while housing
represented approximately 15%.
From the perspective of unit price trends, the unit price of servo systems used in industrial robots
was approximately RMB1,400-RMB1,600 in 2021, declined to approximately RMB1,000-RMB1,200 in
2025, and is expected to further decrease to approximately RMB600-RMB800 by 2030. The unit price of
reducers also showed a downward trend, decreasing from RMB1,800-RMB2,000 in 2021 to RMB800-
RMB1,000 in 2025, and is expected to further decline to around RMB500-RMB600 by 2030. Such price
decreases are mainly driven by continuous technological advancement, increasing localization of core
components and the growing maturity of the supply chain. Overall, as production efficiency of key
components improves and large-scale application accelerates, the unit prices of core components such as
servo systems and reducers are expected to continue to decline, which will help reduce the overall
production cost of industrial robots and provide greater flexibility in setting product selling prices.

OVERVIEW OF CHINA’S COLLABORATIVE ROBOT MARKET
Definition and Classification of Collaborative Robots
Collaborativerobotsarerobotsdesignedtooperatenearhumanswithinasharedworkspace,enabling
direct human-robot interaction or cooperation. Different from the industrial robots, which are primarily
suited for high-precision and high-speed production in isolated environments, collaborative robots are
more suited for the environments involving human interaction and safe collaboration. Based on the
implementation method of mechanical sensing capabilities, collaborative robots can be divided into two
categories:
 Flexible collaborative robots. With native force control capabilities, they feature one built-in
high-precision torque sensor in each joint (six or more in total), enabling global multi-point native
force control. Such robots perform prominently in applications requiring high force perception (e.g.,
precision assembly, flexible grinding, and medical rehabilitation) and possess advantages in safety
and precision. According to the General Technical Requirements for Flexible Control of Industrial
Robots (GB/T 38839-2020) issued by the China Machinery Industry Federation, “flexible control
technology” refers to a class of control methods whereby industrial robots utilize state data fed back
through the drive bus and sensor data collected from external sensors to dynamically adjust motion
planning, enabling point-to-point control or continuous path control. The term “flexible” has been
widely adopted within the collaborative robotics industry.
 Traditionalcollaborativerobots.Theycanachieveforcecontrolfunctionsthroughonlyoneexternal
torque sensor at the end, with relatively concentrated sensing capabilities. They are suitable for
application scenarios with low force control requirements. While traditional collaborative robots
haveadvantagesincostanddeploymentconvenience,theyhavelimitationsinexpandingtocomplex
processes and high-precision compliant operations.
Market Size of Collaborative Robot Industry
Globally,collaborativerobotsaregainingwideradoptionacrossmanufacturingandservicescenarios
due to their advantages in flexible deployment, safe human-robot collaboration and ease of integration.
ThemarketsizeoftheglobalcollaborativerobotmarketreachedRMB9.82billionin2025andisexpected
to further increase to RMB36.08 billion by 2030, representing a CAGR of 29.7% from 2025 to 2030.
China’s collaborative robot market is in a stage of rapid development. The market size of China’s
collaborativerobotsgrewfromRMB2.9billionin2025toRMB11.1billionin2030,ataCAGRof30.7%.
Among them, flexible collaborative robots, with their high compatibility in seamless human-robot
collaboration on production lines, have gradually extended to scenarios with higher complexity and
diversedemand,drivenbybreakthroughsinintelligentforceperceptionandvisiontechnologies.Thesales
revenueofChina’sflexiblecollaborativerobotsincreasedfromRMB0.6billionin2021toRMB1.1billion
in 2025, at a CAGR of 19.8%. Leveraging the advantages of native multi-sensor design in precision,
safety, and flexible operations, the sales revenue of flexible collaborative robots is expected to reach
RMB4.6 billion by 2030, at a CAGR of 32.4% from 2025 to 2030.
In terms of sales volume, the sales volume of China’s collaborative robots increased from 18.0
thousand units in 2021 to 45.9 thousand units in 2025, at a CAGR of 26.4%. The market size is expected
to reach 232.1 thousand units by 2030, at a CAGR of 38.3% from 2025 to 2030. Among these, the sales
volume of flexible collaborative robots is expected to increase from 6.9 thousand units in 2025 to 39.7
thousand units in 2030, representing a CAGR of 42.0%.

 Diversified demand for segmented application scenarios in the manufacturing sector. The

regard the robot industry as a key part of advanced manufacturing and strategic emerging industries
and promote technological innovation and application implementation through long-term plans and
special policies. China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (“MIIT”) issued the
National Intelligent Manufacturing Standards System Construction Guidelines (2024 Edition) (國家
智能製造標準體系建設指南(2024版)), which establishes standards for intelligent equipment such as
collaborative robots in typical industries, aiming to promote their implementation in the smart
manufacturing scenarios.
 Increased demand for safe human-robot collaboration. Under the “human-robot co-line” (人機共線)
productionmodel,enterpriseshavehigherrequirementsforsafetyandflexibilityinthecollaboration
process. By integrating multi-channel torque sensors in each joint and fusing visual and tactile data,
flexible collaborative robots can achieve active obstacle avoidance, anomaly detection, and flexible
response.
Threats and Challenges of China’s Collaborative Robot Industries
 Challengesinbalancingsafetyandperformance.Toenablehuman-robotcollaboration,collaborative
robots are typically required to limit operating speed, output force, and inertia to meet safety
requirements. This may affect production cycle time and operational efficiency to a certain extent,
particularly in high-intensity or high-speed manufacturing scenarios.
 Limitations in payload capacity and operating speed. Due to safety requirements for human-robot
collaboration, collaborative robots are generally designed with constraints on payload capacity and
operating speed. As a result, their applicability in heavy-duty, high-speed, or high-intensity
operational environments may be relatively limited.
Entry Barriers to China’s Collaborative Robot Industries
 Safe collaboration and force-control capabilities. Collaborative robots need to operate safely and
efficiently in shared workspaces with humans. Flexible collaborative robots, in particular, require
advanced joint-level force control, torque sensing and active obstacle avoidance capabilities.
 Talent requirements. Success in the collaborative robot industry requires a diversified talent pool
with expertise in mechanics, electronics and other relevant disciplines. Leading companies have
already established strong R&D teams and talent pipelines. New entrants must invest substantial
capital to attract and cultivate highly skilled professionals in order to build an efficient talent team.
COMPETITIVE OVERVIEW OF CHINA’S INDUSTRIAL ROBOT MARKET
Competitive Landscape of China’s Industrial Robot Providers
China’s industrial robot providers can be broadly categorized into domestic and overseas market
players. Domestic market players often originate from local automation companies or academic research
backgrounds. These providers typically start with indigenous technologies and are characterized by quick
response times and high operational flexibility. Representative domestic industrial robot providers in
China include Estun Automation, EFORT Intelligent Robot and Inovance Technology. The second
category comprises overseas market players, which are generally multinational corporations with a global
presence and possess delivery and service capabilities across multiple countries. Due to intense
competitioninChina,thecompetitivelandscapeamongdomesticprovidersremainsrelativelyfragmented;
however, the market share of domestic players has been gradually increasing. In 2025, domestic market
players accounted for over 20% of the market share in China’s industrial robot market in terms of sales
revenue.

In 2025, in terms of sales revenue, the Company ranked sixth among domestic providers in China’s

OVERVIEW OF THE EMBODIED INTELLIGENT ROBOT MARKET
Definition and Importance of the Embodied Intelligent Robot Industry
Embodied intelligent robots are a new generation of robot form developed with embodied
intelligence as the core concept. They can continuously obtain information through interaction with the
environment, form cognition, and make autonomous decisions, thereby demonstrating a higher level of
adaptability and intelligent behavior.
Among these, embodied intelligent robotic arms represent a key form of embodied intelligent
systems. Compared with traditional industrial or collaborative robotic arms, which primarily perform
pre-programmed and repetitive tasks, embodied intelligent robotic arms integrate multi-modal perception,
– 74 –

=== PAGE 83 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
force control, and adaptive decision-making capabilities. Such systems are able to perceive dynamic
environments, interact with objects with a higher degree of compliance and precision, and continuously
optimize their actions through learning-based methods.
From an industry development perspective, traditional industrial robot providers are actively
expanding into the embodied intelligent robotics field. Leveraging their expertise in actuators, reducers,
control systems, and robotic arms, these providers possess a solid technological foundation to participate
in this market. In particular, industrial robot providers and component suppliers with capabilities in
flexible force control and real-time industrial communication architectures are well positioned to benefit
from the growing adoption of embodied intelligent robots.
Market Size of China’s Embodied Intelligent Robots Industry
China’s embodied intelligent robot market is at a formative stage and only became measurable at
approximately RMB0.6 billion in 2024, yet it is in a stage of rapid growth. The market size of China’s
embodied intelligent robots exceeded RMB3.0 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach approximately
RMB74.3 billion by 2030. Driven by artificial intelligence, multi-modal perception, improved computing
power, and expanded downstream applications, the market is further projected to grow to approximately
RMB460.0 billion by 2035, representing a CAGR of approximately 44.0% from 2030 to 2035, entering
a high-growth phase. Within the next decade, the embodied intelligent robot industry is expected to
becomeanimportantbreakthroughintherobotindustryandartificialintelligenceapplications,promoting
its widespread penetration in multiple fields such as industrial manufacturing, commercial services,
healthcare, and household scenarios.

Drivers and Trends of China’s Embodied Intelligent Robot Industry
 Breakthroughs in multimodal foundation model technologies. Embodied intelligent robots rely on
multimodal perception systems, including vision, voice and force sensing, to acquire and understand
environmental information. Driven by advances in multimodal foundation models, robots can
achieve efficient integration and real-time reasoning of cross-modal information in complex
environments, thereby gaining stronger understanding and decision-making capabilities, breaking
throughthelimitationsoftraditional“repetitivetasks,”andgreatlyenhancingtheirapplicationvalue
in the real world.
 Software-hardware integration and improved computing power. With the advancement of chip
fabrication and the wide application of low-power consumption platforms, the core hardware
performance of embodied intelligent robots has been significantly enhanced. The continuous
upgrading of sensors, drivers, and actuators provides robots with more precise motion control and
higher response speed. At the same time, the software-hardware integrated architecture design
enables robots to achieve efficient data processing and control execution under improved computing
power, reducing energy consumption and latency.
 Dual promotion of capital and policies. China released the Guidelines for the Construction of a
Comprehensive Standardization System for the National Artificial Intelligence Industry (2024
Edition) (國家人工智能產業綜合標準化體系建設指南(2024版)), which identifies embodied
intelligence as a key technological focus and intelligent robots as a priority area for intelligent
products and services. The guidelines aim to drive the implementation of robotic technologies and
applications through a systematic standards framework. Meanwhile, the capital market is also
accelerating its entry. Leading technology companies, industrial funds, and venture capitals are
continuously increasing investment to promote the rapid growth of innovative enterprises.
Threats and Challenges of China’s Embodied Intelligent Robot Industry
 Limited Commercialization. The embodied intelligence robot industry is still in its early exploratory
stage, with a relatively small market scale. Most core products remain in the technology validation
or small-scale pilot phase. A unified commercial model has yet to be established, and profitability
depends on the concurrent advancement of technology maturity, cost reduction, and downstream
demand development. In the short term, enterprises face high investment requirements and long
payback cycles.
 Unproven Application Scenarios. The practical feasibility of embodied intelligence robots in
general-purpose scenarios remains to be tested. The industry currently lacks unified performance
evaluation and safety standards, and product definitions and application boundaries vary widely
among robot providers. Although the policy framework is gradually improving and several leading
enterprises are promoting application pilots, achieving large-scale commercialization still requires
overcoming challenges related to technical stability, cost control, and user adoption.
Entry Barriers to China’s Embodied Intelligent Robot Industry
 System-level R&D and engineering delivery barriers. Embodied intelligent robots are highly
integrated software-hardware systems. Companies need to possess comprehensive system R&D
capabilities and achieve stable, reliable and safe operation in complex real-world scenarios. Leading
industry players have typically accumulated long-term expertise in motion control, perception and
decision-making, safety redundancy and scenario adaptation, making it difficult for new entrants to
replicate in the short term.
 Core components and mass production delivery barriers. Embodied intelligent robots have high
requirementsforcorecomponentsintermsoftorquedensity,responsespeedandsafetylevels,while
also requiring a balance between cost and performance. Companies with in-house development or
– 76 –

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
deep joint development capabilities for core components, quality and reliability validation
capabilities, supply chain management capabilities and mass production yield management
capabilities are better positioned to establish competitive advantages.

This section sets out a summary of certain aspects of laws and regulations of the PRC, which are

PRINCIPAL REGULATORY AUTHORITIES
In addition to the supervision and management by authorities that perform general regulation on
companies in the PRC, the Company’s operations in the PRC are mainly subject to supervision and
management under the following authorities:
MIIT
The main responsibilities of the MIIT include, among others: proposing strategies and policies in
relation to industrial development, drafting and organizing the implementation of industrial plans and
industrial policies, drafting and promulgating industrial regulations and technical specifications,
formulating and implementing standards and policies for high-tech industries, promoting the development
of emerging industries, and guiding relevant industries in strengthening safety production management.
NDRC
The main responsibilities of the NDRC include, among others: organizing the formulation of a
comprehensive industrial policy, regulating and managing fixed-asset investment projects, proposing
strategies and policies for the utilization of inbound and outbound investment, and proposing a negative
list for foreign investment access.
MOFCOM
The main responsibilities of MOFCOM include, among others: supervising and regulating the
foreign investment activities nationwide, formulating foreign investment policies and organizing their
implementation,approvingtheestablishmentofandchangesofforeign-investedenterprisesinaccordance
with applicable laws, promoting industrial restructuring in the distribution sector, guiding reforms in
distribution enterprises, developing commercial services and community commerce, formulating
administrative measures and specific policies for outbound investment, and authorizing, in accordance
with the applicable laws, outbound investment by domestic enterprises.

promulgated on December 31, 2021, effective on March 1, 2022), the regulation applies to the application

algorithm recommendation technologies” as mentioned in the preceding paragraph refers to the use of
algorithm technologies such as generative synthesis, personalized push, ranking selection, retrieval
filtering, and scheduling decision-making to provide information to users. The regulation establish a
unified regulatory framework for Agorithm Recommendation Services. The Algorithm Recommendation
Services providers are required to fulfill primary responsibilities, set up management systems, complete
filing and public disclosure for algorithms with public opinion attributes or social mobilization
capabilities, protect users’ rights and interests, and be subject to hierarchical regulation and security
assessment requirements.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
According to the Administrative Provisions on Deep Synthesis of Internet-based Information
Services (互聯網信息服務深度合成管理規定, Decree No. 12 of the Cyberspace Administration of China,
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and Ministry of Public Security, promulgated on
November 25, 2022, effective on January 10, 2023), the regulation applies to the application of deep
synthesis technology to provide Internet-based information services (hereinafter referred to as the “Deep
Synthesis Services”) within the territory of the PRC. Deep synthesis technology refers to the technology
that uses deep learning, virtual reality, and other generative synthesis algorithms to generate text, images,
audio, video, virtual scenes, and other network information. The regulation requires that the Deep
Synthesis Services providers must assume the primary responsibility for information security, establish
systems for real-name authentication, content review, data security and algorithm governance, label the
generated content, and refrain from engaging in activities that endanger national security, public interests
or the rights and interests of others.
AccordingtotheInterimMeasuresfortheManagementofGenerativeAIServices(生成式人工智能
服務管理暫行辦法, Decree No. 15 of the Cyberspace Administration of China, Promulgated on July 10,
2023, effective onAugust 15, 2023), the regulation applies to the use of generative artificial intelligence
technologies (hereinafter referred to as “Generative AI Technology”) to provide the public within the
territory of the PRC with services of generating contents (hereinafter referred to as “Generative AI
Service”). “Generative AI Technology” is defined as models and related technologies that can generate
text,pictures,audio,videoandothercontents.TheregulationrequirestheGenerativeAIServiceproviders
(i) to conduct data training activities, including pre-training and fine-tuning, and to only use lawfully
sourced data and foundational models, (ii) not to infringe upon the legitimate intellectual property rights
ofothers,(iii)toobtaintherelevantindividual’sconsentorcomplywithothercircumstancesasprescribed
by applicable laws and administrative regulationss while the personal information is processed, (iv) to
adopteffectivemeasurestoimprovetrainingdataqualityandupholdtheauthenticity,accuracy,objectivity
anddiversityoftrainingdata,etc.Besides,theregulationalsosetsforthclearrequirementsgoverningdata
annotation.
Pursuant to theArtificial Intelligence Generated and Synthesized Content Labeling Measures (人工
智能生成合成內容標識辦法,GuoXinBanTongZi[2025]No.2,promulgatedonMarch7,2025,effective
on September 1, 2025)The regulations requires that theAI-generated content (such as images and videos)
must be marked with explicit labels that can be clearly perceived, and implicit labels which are not easily
perceived (such as watermarks). This requirement aims to curb disinformation by ensuring full
transparency and traceability of all AI-generated content.
Our PRC LegalAdviser is of the view that, the major regulations related to artificial intelligence as
listed above mainly focus on utilizing certain technology (i.e. deep synthesis technology, Generative AI
Technology) to generate new content, some further concern about providing the generative new content
or the GenerativeAI Service to the internet users or to the general public within the territory of the PRC.
Based on that: (i) our products and services mainly utilize AI for data analysis and do not involve the
creationofnewcontent,and(ii)weareanenterpriseconcentratingonindustrialrobotsanddonotprovide
Generative AI Service to the general public, nor do we involve the application of certain AI-related
technology (i.e. algorithm recommendation technology) to provide internet information services, our PRC
Legal Adviser is of the view that our business does not involve Generative AI Service or internet
information service utilizing AI-related technology, and therefore the latest regulations governing AI as
listed above are not applicable to us and we are not required to make any filing, registration or obtain
approvals with the relevant PRC authorities for our robots. Should we offer such Generative AI Service
in the future, we commit to complying with the relevant regulations on generativeAI. Moreover, we will
continuously monitor the legislative developments in laws and regulations relating toAI, and timely fulfil
the relevant legal obligations.
REGULATIONS RELATING TO FOREIGN INVESTMENT
According to the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國外商投資法), which was
promulgated by the NPC on March 15, 2019, and coming into effect on January 1, 2020, the state shall
implement the management systems of pre-establishment national treatment and negative list for foreign
investment, and shall give national treatment to foreign investment beyond the negative list.

According to the Measures for the Reporting of Foreign Investment Information (外商投資信息報告
辦法), which was promulgated by the MOFCOM and the SAMR on December 30, 2019 and came into
effect on January 1, 2020, in relation to foreign investors carrying out investment activities directly or
indirectly in the PRC, the foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises shall submit investment
information to the competent commerce authorities pursuant to these measures.
Investment activities in the PRC by foreign investors are principally governed by the Special
Administrative Measures (Negative List) for theAccess of Foreign Investment (2025 Version) (外商投資
准入特別管理措施(負面清單)(2025年版)) (the “Negative List”). The Negative List, which was
promulgated on April 16, 2025, and became effective on the same day, sets out special administrative
measures in respect of the access of foreign investments in a centralized manner. Foreign investors shall
not invest in any field prohibited by the Negative List and shall meet the investment conditions stipulated
for any field restricted by the Negative List, while for foreign investments outside the Negative List, it
shall be administered under the principle of equal treatment to domestic and foreign investment.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
Patent
According to the Patent Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國專利法) promulgated by the SCNPC on
March 12, 1984, and last amended on October 17, 2020 and implemented on June 1, 2021 as well as the
Implementation Rules for the Patent Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國專利法實施細則) promulgated by
the State Council on June 15, 2001, last amended on December 1, 2023 and implemented on January 20,
2024, patents in China are protected by law, the validity period of patent for inventions is 20 years, the
validity period of patent for utility models is 10 years, and the validity period of patent for designs is 15
years, in each case starting from the date of application.
Trademark
According to the Trademark Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國商標法), which was promulgated by
the SCNPC on August 23, 1982, last amended on April 23, 2019 and came into effect on November 1,
2019,andtheImplementationRulesoftheTrademarkLawofthePRC(中華人民共和國商標法實施條例),
whichwaspromulgatedbytheStateCouncilonAugust3,2002,lastamendedonApril29,2014andcame
into effect on May 1, 2014. Registered trademarks are trademarks approved and registered by the
Trademark Office. A trademark registrant enjoys exclusive rights to use a registered trademark, which is
protected by the law.The registration of a trademark shall be valid for ten years from the date of approval
for registration.
Copyright
According to the Copyright Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國著作權法), which was promulgated by
the SCNPC on September 7, 1990, last amended on November 11, 2020 and came into effect on June 1,
2021, and the Implementation Rules of the Copyright Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國著作權法實施條
例), which was promulgated by the State Council on August 2, 2002, last amended on January 30, 2013
and came into effect on March 1, 2013, works of Chinese citizens, legal persons or unincorporated
organizations, i.e. intellectual achievements in the field of literature, art and science that are original and
can be expressed in a certain form, whether published or not, are entitled to copyright. The copyright
holder can enjoy multiple rights, including the right of publication, the right of authorship, and the right
of reproduction.
Domain names
AccordingtotheAdministrativeMeasuresforInternetDomainNames(互聯網域名管理辦法),which
waspromulgatedbytheMIITonAugust24,2017andcameintoeffectonNovember1,2017,theprinciple
of “first come, first served” applies to domain name registration service. The applicant of domain name
registration shall provide the service agency of domain name registration with the true, accurate and
complete information about the domain name holder’s identity for the registration purpose.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO PRODUCT QUALITY
The PRC Product Quality Law (中華人民共和國產品質量法) (the “Product Quality Law”)
promulgated by the SCNPC on February 22, 1993 and most recently amended on December 29, 2018 is
the principal governing law related to the supervision and administration of product quality.According to
the Product Quality Law, manufacturers shall be liable for the quality of products produced by them and
sellers shall take measures to ensure the quality of the products sold by them. A manufacturer shall be
liabletocompensateforanyphysicalinjuriesordamagetopropertyotherthanthedefectiveproductitself
resulting from the defects in the product, unless the manufacturer is able to prove that: (i) the product has
not been put into circulation; (ii) the defects causing injuries or damage did not exist at the time when the
product was put into circulation; or (iii) the science and technology at the time when the product was put
into circulation were at a level incapable of detecting the existence of the defect. A seller shall be liable
to compensate for any physical injuries or damage to property of others caused by the defects in the
product.Where a product is defective due to a mistake made by the seller and such defect causes physical
injury or damage to the property of others, the seller shall bear liability for compensation. Where a seller
cannot specify the producer of a defective product nor the supplier of such defective product, the seller
shallbeliableforcompensation.Whereadefectinaproductcausesphysicalinjuriestoothersordamages
to the property of others, the victim may claim compensation from the producer of the product or from
the seller of the product.
Pursuant to the Civil Code of the PRC (中華人民共和國民法典) (the “Civil Code”) promulgated by
the NPC on May 28, 2020 and becoming effective on January 1, 2021, in the event of damages caused to
others due to the defects in a product, the infringed party may seek compensation from the manufacturer
or the seller of such product and shall have the right to request the manufacturer and the seller to bear
tortious liabilities, such as cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, elimination of danger, etc.

2019 and January 1, 2020, respectively. Pursuant to the LandAdministration Law, state-owned land may
be transferred or allocated to construction entities or individuals in accordance with the law.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO TAXATION
Income tax
AccordingtotheEnterpriseIncomeTaxLawofthePRC(中華人民共和國企業所得稅法),whichwas
promulgated by the SCNPC on March 16, 2007 with effect from January 1, 2008 and last amended on
December 29, 2018, and the Regulations on the Implementation of the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the
PRC(中華人民共和國企業所得稅法實施條例),whichwaspromulgatedbytheStateCouncilonDecember
6, 2007 with effect from January 1, 2008 and amended on December 6, 2024, all domestic enterprises in
China (including foreign-invested enterprises) shall be subject to enterprise income tax (EIT) at the
uniform tax rate of 25%, except for the high-tech enterprises provided by the State, which will be subject
to enterprise income tax at the reduced rate of 15%, or the qualified small low-profit enterprises, which
will enjoy the reduced EIT rate of 20%.
Enterprises that are recognized as high-tech enterprises in accordance with the Administrative
MeasuresonAccreditationofHigh-techEnterprises(高新技術企業認定管理辦法)areentitledtoenjoythe
preferential EIT rate of 15%. The validity period of the high-tech enterprise qualification shall be three
years from the date of issuance of the certificate of high-tech enterprise.
According to the Announcement on EIT Policies for Promoting High-quality Development of
Integrated Circuit Industry and Software Industry (關於促進集成電路產業和軟件產業高質量發展企業所

部)(the“MOF”),theSAT,theNDRCandtheMIITonDecember11,2020andcameintoeffectonJanuary
1, 2020, the qualified integrated circuit design, equipment, materials, packaging, testing and software
enterprises enjoy the EIT exemption for the first two years starting from the first profit-making year of
the enterprise, and a half-rate reduction of the EIT of 25% from the third to the fifth year (that is 12.5%).

Value-added tax
According to the Interim Regulations of the PRC on Value-added Tax (中華人民共和國增值稅暫行
條例), which was promulgated by the State Council on December 13, 1993 and implemented on January
1, 1994, and last revised on November 19, 2017, has come into effect on the same date and the Detailed
Rules for the Implementation of the Interim Regulations of the PRC on Value-added Tax (中華人民共和
國增值稅暫行條例實施細則), which was promulgated by the Ministry of Finance on December 25, 1993
and last amended and effective on October 28, 2011, entities and individuals that sell goods or labor
services of processing, repair or replacement, sell services, intangible assets, or immovables, or import
goods within the territory of Chinese Mainland are taxpayers of value-added tax, and shall pay VAT in
accordance with law. Unless otherwise stipulated, the VAT rate is 17% for taxpayers selling goods, labor
services, or tangible movable property leasing services or importing goods; 11% for taxpayers selling
transportation, postal, basic telecommunications, construction, or immovable leasing services, selling
immovables, transferring land use rights, or selling or importing specific goods; unless otherwise
stipulated, 6% for taxpayers selling services or intangible assets.
According to the Circular of the MOF and the SAT on Adjusting Value-added Tax Rate (財政部、
稅務總局關於調整增值稅稅率的通知), which was promulgated by the MOF and the SATonApril 4, 2018
and became effective on May 1, 2018, the tax rates for the taxable sales or goods import activity, which
were subject to the tax rates of 17% and 11% respectively, were adjusted to 16% and 10% respectively.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO LABOR CONTRACT, SOCIAL INSURANCE AND
HOUSING PROVIDENT FUND
Labor Law and Labor Contract Law
According to the Labor Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國勞動法), which was promulgated by the
SCNPC on July 5, 1994, came into effect on January 1, 1995 and last revised on December 29, 2018, and
the Labor Contract Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國勞動合同法), which was promulgated on June 29,
2007 and has come into effect on January 1, 2008, revised on December 28, 2012 and came into effect on
July 1, 2013, written labor contracts shall be executed between an entity and its employees if an
employment relationship is established. Employers are required to inform their employees about their job
responsibilities,workingconditions,occupationalhazards,remunerationandothermatterswithwhichthe
employees may be concerned. Employers shall pay remuneration to employees on time and in full in
accordance with the commitments set forth in their employment contracts and the relevant PRC laws and
regulations.
Social Insurance and Housing Provident Fund
Pursuant to the Social Insurance Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國社會保險法), which was
promulgated by the SCNPC on October 28, 2010, came into effect on July 1, 2011 and last revised on
December29,2018,theInterimRegulationsonCollectionandPaymentofSocialInsurancePremiums(社
會保險費徵繳暫行條例),whichwaspromulgatedbytheStateCouncilonJanuary22,1999andrevisedon
March 24, 2019, the Trial Measures for Enterprise Staff Maternity Insurance (企業職工生育保險試行辦
法),whichwaspromulgatedbytheMinistryofHumanResourcesandSocialSecurityandcameintoeffect
on January 1, 1995, the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance (工傷保險條例), which was
promulgated by the State Council and came into effect on January 1, 2004, amended on December 20,
2010 and came into effect on January 1, 2011, and the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident
Fund (住房公積金管理條例), which was promulgated and implemented on April 3, 1999 and last revised
on March 24, 2019, employers in Chinese Mainland shall provide their employees with welfare schemes
coveringbasicpensioninsurance,basicmedicalinsurance,unemploymentinsurance,maternityinsurance,
occupational injury insurance and housing provident fund. Employers who fail to contribute to the above
social insurance may be ordered by the social insurance premiums collection authority to make full
payment within a prescribed time period; if the employer fails to do so, a fine may be imposed. If an
employing entity fails to make the payment towards housing provident funds within a prescribed time
limit, an application may be made to a people’s court for enforcement.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO FOREIGN EXCHANGE
Pursuant to the Regulations on Foreign Exchange Control of the PRC (中華人民共和國外匯管理條
例) promulgated by the State Council on January 29, 1996 and came into effect onApril 1, 1996, and last
amended on August 5, 2008 and came into effect on the same date, and relevant regulations, there is no
restriction on the recurring international payment and transfer. Foreign exchange income and expenses of
capitalitems(suchasdirectequityinvestmentandloans)shallcomplywiththeprovisionsofrelevantlaws
and regulations, and where required for approval or registration by relevant regulations from foreign
exchange administration authorities, such approval or registration shall be filed.
According to the Notice on Relevant Issues Concerning theAdministration of Foreign Exchange for
Overseas Listing (關於境外上市外匯管理有關問題的通知) promulgated by the SAFE on February 1,
2005, as amended on December 26, 2014 by the SAFE Circular 16 (defined below), the domestic
companies shall register the overseas listing with the foreign exchange control bureau located at its
registered address in 15 working days after completion of the overseas listing and issuance.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
According to the Notice of the SAFE on Reforming the Management Mode of Foreign Exchange
Capital Settlement of Foreign Investment Enterprises (國家外匯管理局關於改革外商投資企業外匯資本金
結匯管理方式的通知) promulgated on March 30, 2015, came into effect on June 1, 2015 and as amended
bytheSAFECircular16(definedbelow),partiallyabolishedonDecember30,2019andpartiallyamended
on March 23, 2023, foreign-invested enterprises could settle their foreign exchange capital on a
discretionary basis according to the actual needs of their business operations. Whilst, foreign-invested
enterprises are prohibited to use the foreign exchange capital settled in RMB (a) for any expenditures
beyondthebusinessscopeoftheforeign-investedenterprisesorforbiddenbylawsandregulations;(b)for
direct or indirect securities investment; (c) to provide entrusted loans (unless permitted in the business
scope), repay loans between enterprises (including advances by third parties) or repay RMB bank loans
that have been on-lent to a third party; and (d) to purchase real estates not for self-use purposes (save for
real estate enterprises).
According to the Circular of the SAFE on Optimizing Foreign Exchange Management Service in
Support of Foreign Business Development (國家外匯管理局關於優化外匯管理支持涉外業務發展的通知)
promulgated by the SAFE on April 10, 2020 and came into effect on the same day, on the premise of
ensuring the authentic and compliant use of funds and complying with the existing regulations on the use
of capital income, eligible enterprises are allowed to use capital income such as capital funds, foreign
debts and proceeds from overseas listing for domestic payments without providing materials to the bank
in advance for authenticity verification on a case-by-case basis. The concerned banks shall follow the
principle of prudent development to control the relevant business risks and conduct post inspection on the
use of funds under capital accounts handled in accordance with relevant requirements.
In accordance with the Circular on Further Promoting Cross-border Trade and Investment
Facilitation (國家外匯管理局關於進一步促進跨境貿易投資便利化的通知), which was issued and came
into effect on October 23, 2019 by the SAFE and was amended on December 4, 2023, foreign-invested
enterpriseengagedinnon-investmentbusinessarepermittedtosettleforeignexchangecapitalinRMBand
make domestic equity investments with such RMB funds according to laws and regulations under the
condition that the current SpecialAdministrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign InvestmentAccess
are not violated and the relevant domestic investment projects are true and compliant.
REGULATIONS RELATING TO OVERSEAS DIRECT INVESTMENT
Pursuant to theAdministrative Measures for Outbound Investment by Enterprises (企業境外投資管
理辦法) promulgated by the NDRC on December 26, 2017 and came into effect on March 1, 2018, the
investing activities of enterprises in Chinese Mainland such as acquiring overseas ownerships, controlling
rights, operating and management rights and other relevant interests by way of investing assets and
interests or providing financing and guarantees to control its overseas enterprises, either directly or
indirectly, are required to obtain approval or filing with the NDRC in accordance with the relevant
conditions of the overseas investment projects. Outbound investment projects that involve sensitive
countriesandregionsorsensitiveindustriesshallbesubjecttoadministrationofverificationandapproval
by the NDRC.
Pursuant to the Measures for theAdministration of Overseas Investment (境外投資管理辦法) which
was issued by the MOFCOM on September 6, 2014 and came into effect on October 6, 2014, the
MOFCOM and the commerce departments at provincial levels shall subject the overseas investment of
enterprises to recordation or confirmation management, depending on the actual circumstances of
investment. Overseas investment involving any sensitive country or region, or any sensitive industry shall
be subject to confirmation management. Overseas investment under other circumstances shall be subject
to recordation management.
Pursuant to the Regulations on the Foreign Exchange Administration of the Overseas Direct
Investment of Domestic Institutions (境內機構境外直接投資外匯管理規定) issued by the SAFE on July
13, 2009 and came into effect on August 1, 2009 and the Notice of the State Administration of Foreign
Exchange on Further Simplifying and Improving the Foreign Exchange Management Policies for Direct
Investment, when obtaining approval for overseas investment, Chinese enterprises must apply to the bank
of their registered location for foreign exchange registration for overseas direct investment.
