Our R&D Process
Our R&D process involves a framework in which factors such as customers demand, feasibility
analysis, technology developments and application scenarios are taken into consideration. The diagram
below sets out the principal steps which we generally follow in our research and development process.
Concept Planning Development Verification Launch
Request for System Preliminary Detailed Pilot Mass
Prototype
product specifications design design production production
Our R&D process mainly includes (1) conceptual stage, (2) planning stage, (3) development stage
and (4) verification and commercialization stage.
Conceptualstage.Conceptualstageincludesthepreparatorystagesfromdemandplanningtoproject
establishment. In this stage, our product planning department conducts demand research and data analysis
aswellasmarketandtechnicalfeasibilityanalysis,andsubmitsrelevantresearchanddevelopmentproject
establishment application for management’s review.
Planning stage. Planning stage includes the stages from system requirements defining to review of
system and design summary. In this stage, our research and development department breaks down the
system requirements in detail based on the information submitted by the product planning department in
the conceptual stage, and completes summaries of design document for each module, including structure,
components, software and algorithm, among others, to determine the technical benchmark for the entire
product development.
Development and testing stage. Development and testing stage includes the stages from detailed
designing to prototype testing review. In this stage, our research and development staff carry out detailed
designing based on summaries of design document for each module from the planning stage. After a
review for detailed designing process, we arrange proofing for sample components, and use those
components to assemble prototype. At the same time, the testing department specifies the system testing
specifications to test and verify the prototype.
– 148 –

=== PAGE 157 ===
BUSINESS
Verificationandlaunchstage.Verificationandlaunchstageincludesthestagesfromtrialproduction
review to commercialization. During the trial production review, we determine whether to carry out small
batch trial production of relevant products. Based on the trial production results, we further determine
whether to proceed with mass production, which represents the commercialization of relevant products.
As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had not in-licensed any material intellectual properties,
outsourced any R&D process to, or undertaken any R&D in collaboration with external third parties.
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

the following key measures to protect our intellectual property rights, including: (1) implementing a set

an intellectual property task force to guide, manage, supervise and monitor our daily work regarding

action in timely manner if any potential conflicts with our intellectual property rights are identified, and

As advised by our PRC LegalAdvisor, pursuant to the Patent Law of the People’s Republic of China
(中華人民共和國專利法), an invention patent registered in China is valid for a term of 20 years from the
date of filing of the application for the patent, an utility model patent registered in China is valid for a
term of 10 years from the date of filing of the application for the patent, and a design patent registered
in China is valid for a term of 15 years from the date of filing of the application for the patent. Despite
our precautions, however, third parties may obtain and use our intellectual property without our consent.
Unauthorized use of our intellectual property by third parties and the expenses incurred in protecting our

Products and Solutions.” Our Directors confirm that we did not have any material disputes or any other
pending material legal proceedings of intellectual property rights with third parties during the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.
OUR SALES NETWORK
We have built up a customer base in Chinese Mainland and overseas across over 40 countries and
regions. We sell our robots and related robotic solutions through primarily direct sales, and to a lesser
extent, sell our robots to distributors. Our major customers are primarily engaged in manufacturing
hardware, industrial equipment and components, as well as the provision of system integration services.

BUSINESS
During the Track Record Period, our direct sales team sold both robotic products and robotic
solutions. In general, robotic products are relatively higher-margin, standardized products, whereas
robotic solutions are relatively lower-margin and customized in various degrees. In contrast, our
distributors focused exclusively on selling robotic products, resulting in a relatively higher gross profit
margin for the distributorship channel compared to the direct sales channel.
Direct Sales
We had 550, 776 and 1,116 direct sales customers in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Our direct
sales customers mainly comprise enterprise customers in the manufacturing, commercial services and
healthcare sectors. We also sell robots to system integrators, which incorporate our robots into their own
automation solutions. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the revenue generated from direct sales was RMB246.8
million, RMB271.3 million and RMB460.7 million, respectively, representing 92.4%, 83.4% and 88.3%
of our total revenue in the same periods, respectively.
We directly manage our direct sales force as we consider them as our key way to build our brand
image by interacting, introducing and demonstrating the features of our products and solutions directly to
our customers. Our sales team, which consisted of 136 members as of the Latest Practicable Date, is
equipped with knowledge of our products and solutions and is primarily responsible for frequently
communicating with our customers and understanding their feedback on the quality, preferences,
improvements and market demand of our products and solutions. They play an important part in the
planning, development and implementation of our planned marketing strategies. To encourage and
incentivize our direct sales force, we have implemented a compensation structure that includes a fixed
componentaswellasaperformance-basedcomponentandalsosetperformancetargetsforoursalesteam.
Principal terms of sales agreements with direct sales customers
We typically enter into sales agreements with our direct customers. The following paragraphs set
forth a summary of the salient terms of our arrangements with direct sales customers.
Product details. Our sales to our direct sales customers are primarily case-by-case and our contracts
are drafted for each purchase of our robotic products or other accessories by our direct sales customers.
Wearerequiredtosupplythepurchasedproductswithinthetimeperiodindicatedinourcontractwithour
direct sales customers or we may face material punishment of contract depending on the content of the
original agreement.
Product specification. Our customers typically set forth specific product specification requirements
for the products ordered, including the type and specific model of our robotic product, additional
components of the model purchased if applicable, number of products, price per unit and the total price.
Productdeliveryandtransferofliability.Typically,weareresponsiblefordeliveringproductstothe
customer’s designated location and may be liable for damages to the products caused during
transportation.Liabilitypassestoourdirectsalescustomersoncetheproductshavebeendeliveredtotheir
specified location.
Pricing policy. We sell our products to direct sales customers according to the terms of the
agreements.
Payment term. We typically require payment in two installments: an initial 50% of the purchase
amount is paid upon signing the contract, followed by the second half of the purchase amount upon the
receipt of the ordered products.

Credit term. We typically offer a credit period up to 180 days to our direct sales customers.
Supporting services. We are responsible for providing supporting services to the direct sales
customers. We provide two days of free domestic in-person training services to our customers after the
acknowledgment of receipt and are responsible for the installation and the commission of our robotic
products.
Product warranty, return and exchange. Our direct sales customers are required to verify the
products received and provide receipt confirmation within three business days. Our product warranty
period is generally 12 months and begins on the day of arrival at the delivery location. If our direct sales
customers receive defective products that malfunction due to flaws in materials, design, or workmanship,
we shall replace the faulty items free of charge or provide repairs at no cost.
Confidentiality. Each party shall not disclose the content of the contract, disseminate confidential
information including but not limited to our trade secrets, blueprints, product specifications and user
information and further distribute or sell our products without consent.
Intellectual property rights. We retain complete ownership to all intellectual property rights to any
work products generated during the performance of our sales contract. Our direct sales customers are
restricted from transferring any information relating to intellectual properties to third parties.
Termination. Generally, the contract can be terminated upon mutual agreement. If either party
cancels the agreement unilaterally, it may be subject to termination fees.
Distributors
Weselectivelyengagedistributorstomarketourrobots.Weleveragetheirexperienceandknowledge
of the target markets as well as their existing sales network and resources. This approach allows us to
expand our market reach over a wider geographical area and achieve deeper market penetration than if we
had relied solely on direct sales and marketing. This strategy also helps us avoid substantial sales and
marketing costs, create synergy with our products and solutions, expand our industry presence, and
enhance our brand recognition. As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we engaged 33, 55 and 43
distributors, respectively. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the revenue generated from our distributors was
RMB20.2 million, RMB53.9 million and RMB61.0 million, respectively, representing 7.6%, 16.6% and
11.7%ofourtotalrevenueinthesameperiods,respectively.AccordingtotheCICReport,theengagement
of distributors for the sales of robotic products is industry norm in the robotics industry.
We select new distributors throughout the year and conduct annual assessment of existing
distributors. We have implemented rigorous selection criteria for new distributors to ensure that they are
well equipped to represent our brand and promote our products. We also conduct a stringent annual
assessmenttoreviewourbusinessrelationshipswithexistingdistributors.Ourprimaryevaluationcriteria,
among others, are the actual annual purchase amount as well as advertising and marketing activities.
During the Track Record Period, we terminated cooperation with certain distributors primarily due to (1)
their inability to meet certain agreed-upon sales targets, and (2) instances of cross-regional sales which
caused disruptions in our pricing system. Meanwhile, we also terminated distributors as a result of
strategic adjustments to our sales channels to enhance cost-effectiveness. In 2025, we terminated
relationshipswith19distributorsthatwereinareasoflow-efficiencies,andprioritizedcollaborationswith
distributorsthatmayhelptofacilitateourexpansionintonewapplicationscenarios.In2023and2024,the
amount of non-recurring historical sales from distributors was RMB0.1 million and RMB0.7 million,
respectively,whichwereimmaterialcomparedtoourtotalrevenuegeneratedfromdistributorsinthesame
periods.

BUSINESS
Our relationship with distributors is categorized as seller-buyer relationships, as they buy out our
products from us and then resell the products to the end customers. We recognize sales revenues from
distributors when the control over our products is transferred to such distributors. We generally allow
returns and/or exchanges for limited circumstances, such as quality defects or damages during
transportation. Our return policy is generally in line with common industry practice, according to the CIC
Report. Our distributors are not allowed to sub-distribute our products to other parties without our prior
consent.We offer sales discounts to our distributors on a case-by-case basis, taking into account of annual
sales volume. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we were not aware
of any sub-distributors of our products.
We have implemented internal control measures to prevent channel stuffing. Specifically, we do not
allow our distributors to proactively stock our products, and we regularly track our distributors’ inventory
and sales progress through phone calls, emails, and on-site visits.

We typically enter into distribution agreements with our distributors. The following paragraphs set

products within the predetermined geographic area.
Term. The term of the distribution agreement is typically one year.
Obligations. Our distributors shall promote and sell our products within the predetermined

Product delivery and transfer of liability. We are responsible for delivering products to the
distributors’ designated locations and may be liable for damages to the products caused during
transportation. Liability passes to our distributors once the products have been delivered to their specified
location.
Pricing policy. Distributors set the selling prices of our products to the end customers based on our
suggested price.
Payment term. We typically require our distributors to make full payment before the delivery of our
products.
Credit term. We typically offer a credit period up to 30 days to our distributors.
Sales amount and sales target. The distributors confirm the purchase amount with us in written
purchase orders specifying product model, specifications, quantity and total amount.
Product warranties. We warrant that our products shall be free from defects in material and
workmanship under normal use generally for a period of 12 months from the date of delivery.
Return and Exchange policy. We allow returns or exchanges only for defective products that
malfunction due to flaws in materials, design, or workmanship. We may allow exchange free of charge
upon distributors’ timely notification of any discrepancy in product specifications, or compromised
packaging rendering products commercially unusable at delivery.
Minimum sales requirements. We require an annual minimum sales number of robots and may
terminate the distributorship for any failure to comply with this requirement.
Intellectual property rights. We retain complete ownership to all intellectual property rights to any
work products generated during the performance of our sales contract. Our distributors are restricted from
transferring any information relating to intellectual properties to third parties.
Termination. Parties may terminate the distribution agreement in the event of either party breaches
any material term or condition after written notice.
SALES AND MARKETING
Weconstantlyseektoexploretheapplicationscenariosofproductsthroughmaintainingandbuilding
relationships with our existing or new customers. We have adopted multi-faceted marketing initiatives,
including digital marketing and industry exhibitions, among others.As a key component of our marketing
strategies, we demonstrate the capabilities of our products and solutions and share our experience and
knowledge of our products and solutions with our customers, and therefore, we often engage with our
community through a wide variety of content on the mainstream social media and our official website,
with the goal of creating interactive exchanges with our customers, thereby promoting and sharing the
information of our products and solutions. Additionally, we have been actively participating in various
industry exhibitions and trade shows, which provides us with the opportunity to showcase our products
and solutions to prospective customers. We also seek to play an active role in industry associations
underlying the various application scenarios our products and solutions target, which allows us to stay
informed of the latest developments in the relevant fields.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our selling and marketing expenses were RMB54.9 million, RMB63.0
million and RMB75.6 million, respectively, representing 20.6%, 19.4% and 14.6% of our revenue for the
same periods, respectively.

BACKLOG
Backlog represents our estimate of contract value that remains to be completed as of a certain date.
New order/project value represents the amount that we expect to receive under the terms of the contract,
assuming the contract is performed in accordance with its terms. To the extent the work under these
contracts advances, amounts are progressively removed from backlog. Backlog is not an audited measure
defined by HKFRS and our methodology in determining backlog may not be comparable to the
methodology used by other companies.
Backlog might not be indicative of our future operating results and difficulties in contract
performance could lead to inaccuracies with respect to the ultimate income from uncompleted contracts.
The termination or modification of any one or more sizeable contracts or the addition of other contracts
could have a substantial and immediate effect on the amount of our backlog and the revenue and profits
we may earn from such contracts, and could have a material adverse effect on our profitability and
financial condition.As a result, our backlog information presented in this prospectus should not be relied
on as an indicator of our future earnings.

value less our recognized revenue for the year equals our backlog at the end of the year.

OUR CUSTOMERS
As a China-based company, we have established and continue to forge relationships with domestic
and international companies across different industry sectors. To this end, we analyze customer dynamics
and market trends in key sectors to seek more opportunities across industries, which allows us to enlarge
the use cases of our offerings and our customer base. We have a broad and growing customer base, which
coverstheChinesedomesticmarketandapproximately40overseascountriesandregionsinEurope,other
Asian markets, Americas, and Africa, supporting the technological upgrades to intelligent automation by
our overseas customers. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our overseas revenue was RMB38.2 million, RMB29.2
million and RMB46.6 million, respectively, accounting for 14.3%, 9.0% and 8.9% of our revenue for the
same years, respectively. During the Track Record Period, we recorded relatively higher gross profit and
gross profit margin for our overseas customers as compared to those of our domestic customers, primarily
due to the higher prices that we had set for our overseas customers, as a result of a lower level of
competition for our products in the overseas market. Our major customers are primarily engaged in
manufacturing hardware, industrial equipment and components, as well as the provision of system
integration services.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue from the five largest customers in each year during the Track

OUR SUPPLIERS
Our suppliers primarily consist of China-based providers of materials, components and relevant
servicesfortheproductionofourrobots.Weprimarilyprocurehardwareaccessoriesforrobotproduction,
such as castings and machine parts, speed reducers, and electric motors from our major suppliers. We
select leading suppliers in the relevant fields in order to ensure the availability and quality of such
materials, components and services. Our procurement process is under periodic review for higher
efficiency and cost control purpose without jeopardizing the quality of deliverables.
The key materials and components for our robots and robotic solutions primarily include castings
and machine parts, speed reducers, servo motors, cables, sensors, and other components. We require the
suppliers to develop and manufacture the components based on our specifications with quality standards
satisfactory to us. Upon receiving the components, we retain the right to reject or return based on the
resultsofourinspection.Wetypicallyobtainquotationsfrommultiplesuppliers,inordertoensuresupply
stability and optimal procurement cost control, whereas we may source those components which we
believe substitute suppliers can be easily identified. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we had not experienced significant difficulties in maintaining sources of supplies and
expect to be able to maintain adequate sources of quality supplies in the future.
Wenormallyenterintomasteragreementswithprovidersofmaterialsandcomponentswhichsetout
the general terms and conditions of cooperation. We make separate purchase orders pursuant to the
framework agreements and finalize prices and volumes with each purchase order. We make the payment
as set forth in the purchase order, and the supplier is typically responsible for the delivery of the products.
Priortoenteringintobusinessrelationshipswithprovidersofsuchmaterialsandcomponents,weevaluate
a variety of factors, including their product quality, qualification, reputation, pricing and overall services.
We perform thorough due diligence on our suppliers, request samples before making purchase orders, and
regularly monitor and review their performance.
We have established a procurement team to arrange and place orders for our major procurements,
including materials, equipment and devices and modules. Our procurement team are responsible for
formulating our procurement plans, development, evaluations and management of suppliers, demand
analysis, price comparison and negotiation and procurement cost management.We have also implemented
systematic procurement procedures focused on bulk and online procurements to enhance our efficiency.
We have adopted supplier qualification procedures to standardize our supplier selection process. In
selectingoursuppliers,weprimarilyconsiderfactorsincludingproductquality,deliverycapabilities,price
level, technical and reputation. We formulate and continually update our qualified supplier list and
evaluate our supplier status from time to time. We also implement rigorous quality control procedures for
our supplies. For details, see “—Quality Control.”

Our Directors confirm that we had not experienced any significant material fluctuation in prices set
by our suppliers, material breach of contract on the part of our suppliers or delay in delivery of our orders
from our suppliers during the Track Record Period. As of the Latest Practicable Date, none of our

Principal terms of supplier agreements
The following paragraphs set forth a summary of the salient terms of our arrangements with
suppliers.
Product delivery. Suppliers are generally responsible for delivering the products that meet the
original manufacturer’s quality standards to our designated locations in accordance with the agreed
delivery schedule.
Payment term. Payments are subject to satisfactory completion of our inspection process and formal
acceptance of the delivered products. We typically pay our suppliers in installments: an initial proportion
of the purchase amount is paid upon signing the contract, another proportion paid prior to delivery, a third
proportion following satisfactory inspection, and a final proportion after the 12-month warranty period.
Credit term. Suppliers typically grant us a credit term of up to 90 days.
Warranty period. Suppliers generally provide us with a warranty period of 12 months from the date
of acceptance of the supplied products.
Return and exchange policy. Suppliers are typically responsible for repair, exchange or returns of
product if quality issues arise within the warranty period.
Intellectual property rights. Suppliers generally guarantee that the supplied products are not in
breach of any intellectual property rights of third parties.
Termination. Parties may terminate the supplier agreement upon mutual agreement.
Overlapping of Major Customers and Suppliers
During the Track Record Period, one of our major customers, CustomerA, was also our supplier for
simulation software. In each year during the Track Record Period, the purchase amount from CustomerA
was approximately RMB2.2 thousand, RMB2.2 thousand and RMB3.1 thousand, respectively,
representing 0.001%, 0.001% and 0.001% of our cost of sales in the same periods, respectively.
During the Track Record Period, five of our major suppliers, including Supplier A, Supplier B,
Supplier D, Supplier E and Supplier G, were also our customers for robotic products and spare parts. The
suppliers generally purchased our robots for their production lines. In each year during the Track Record

and RMB1.0 million, representing 0.02%, 0.03% and 0.2% of our total revenue in the same years,
respectively. Specifically, Supplier A purchased industrial and collaborative robots from us in 2024, and
the gross profit generated from it was RMB37.2 thousand in the same year, with a gross profit margin of
34.5% in the same year. Supplier B purchased industrial robots and robotic spare parts from us in 2025,

OUR PRODUCTION
During the Track Record Period, we manufactured and produced our robotic products through our
production facilities in Jining, Shandong Province. Prior to the establishment of our first production
facilities in 2022, we started self-production in 2017 in leased facilities.
We formulate production schedules and plans according to the market demand, taking into
consideration with the level of our stock and utilization rates of our production facilities. We have
implementedasetofinternalproductionandoperationpoliciesincompliancewiththeapplicablenational
and international industry standards. We carry out regular inspections to assess the conditions of our
production facilities and conduct necessary repairs and maintenance.
Our Production Processes
The following diagram illustrates the principal steps of the production process generally applicable
to our robotic products.

Posture correction

BUSINESS
Assembly stage.We generally start the production process of our robotic product by first assembling
the essential robotics components to form the core body of the product. Depending on the type of product
beingproducedandthefunctionalitiesrequired,thecorebodyisfurtherimportedwithvariousparameters.
Testing stage.After we assemble all of the required components for our robotic product, an overall
completeness check is performed to ensure that all components have been properly assembled, and
necessary software checks are also carried out at this stage.An overall functionality test is then conducted
to test whether the product could perform all of its intended functions properly. The next step is posture
correction, where we perform more specific tests and carry out necessary adjustments to ensure the
accuracy of the physical postures and movements of the product.
Packaging stage. The finished robotic products are packaged and transported to the warehouses for
final delivery.

Our inventories include raw materials and consumables, working in progress, finished goods.As of
December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, our inventories were RMB99.3 million, RMB86.5 million and
RMB195.2 million, respectively.We have a strict inventory control policy to monitor our inventory levels
in order to minimize obsolete inventory. Through close coordination with our customers and our
third-party contract manufacturers, we are able to carry less raw materials and in-process inventories and
lower our inventory risk.
We review the condition of our inventories at the end of each reporting period and makes provisions
against inventory items based on estimates of the realizable value with reference to the latest sale prices
and current market conditions. based on sales forecasts. Sales forecasts are prepared based on agreements
or orders on hand and estimated sales in the foreseeable future based on historical experiences with our
customers and current market conditions of the robot industry. Management estimates the net realizable
value for inventories based primarily on the latest invoice prices and current market conditions. The
estimation is reassessed at the end of each reporting period.The provision against inventories requires the
use of judgments and estimates. Where the actual outcome or expectation in future is different from the
original estimate, such difference will impact on the carrying value of inventories and the write-down of
inventories recognized in the periods in which such estimates have been changed.
We also conduct detailed sales forecasts taking into consideration of factors such as sales strategy,
historical sales data, industry changes, inventory levels of finished goods, and supply chain risks and
conduct regular checks and reviews on the performance of distributors and provide supports to
underperformed distributors.

THIRD-PARTY PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS
Background
During the Track Record Period, certain our customers (individually or collectively, the “Relevant
Customers”) settled payments with us through accounts that do not belong to the contractual parties under
the corresponding sales and purchase agreements (the “Third-Party Payment Arrangements”). The
Relevant Customers during theTrack Record Period primarily consisted of customers in the form of small
limited companies.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the number of the Relevant Customers was nil, ten and three, respectively.
Among them, most of the third-party payors of such Relevant Customers during the Track Record Period
were affiliates of the respective Relevant Customers, and only the third-party payors of two Relevant
Customers in the year ended December 31, 2025 were independent from the respective Relevant
Customers.
– 175 –

=== PAGE 184 ===
BUSINESS
The aggregate amount they settled under the Third-Party Payment Arrangements was nil, RMB1.6
million and RMB0.7 million, respectively, which accounted for nil, 0.5% and 0.1% of our total revenue,
respectively, in the same periods. No individual Relevant Customer has made material contribution to our
revenue during the Track Record Period.
To the best of knowledge of our Directors, the Relevant Customers chose to settle through the
Third-Party Payment Arrangements primarily due to payment convenience and faster transaction cycle.
Termination and Implication of Third-Party Payment Arrangements
We ceased the Third-Party Payment Arrangements in September 2025. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, none of our customers utilized the Third-Party Payment Arrangements to settle payments with us.
We consider that the termination of the Third-party Payment Arrangements did not have, nor will
have, any material adverse effect on the liquidity, business operation and financial performance of the
Group, primarily because the aggregate amount they settled under theThird-Party PaymentArrangements
was immaterial.
As advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, (1) since our third-party payments are grounded in genuine
lawful transactions and commercially prudent arrangements and there is no intention to conceal, falsify,
or misrepresent any proceeds of crime or the source and nature of income derived from such proceeds, the
risks were low for our Group to be found obligated to return funds to Relevant Customers or their
designated third-party payors under theThird-Party PaymentArrangements; and (2) our Company has not
been found to be involved in any money laundering activities, activities that could be related to money
laundering or any relevant investigations, and as such, the risk of the Third-Party PaymentArrangements
being deemed as constituting the crime of money laundering underArticle 191 of the Criminal Law of the
PRC(中華人民共和國刑法)forthepurposeofcoveringuporconcealingthesourceandnatureofproceeds
or gains is low.
Based on the foregoing, our Directors confirm that, to the best of their knowledge and based on the
know-your-customer procedures and internal control measures implemented, during the Track Record
Period, the relevant payments were based on bona fide underlying transactions and valid contractual
relationships, and there were no instances of commercial bribery, money laundering, tax evasion, or
existing or potential disputes with our Group related to the Third-Party Payment Arrangements.
Enhanced Internal Control Measures of Third-Party Payment Arrangements
To safeguard our interest against risks associated with Third-Party Payment Arrangements, since
September 2025, we have significantly enhanced and implemented various internal control measures in
order to rectify the Third-Party Payment Arrangements. Our efforts to rectify the Third-Party Payment
Arrangements include, among other things:
 We initiated the implementation of rectification measures and informed our employees
regarding the enhanced internal control measures.
 Westrictlyprohibitcustomersfromusingthird-partyaccountsforpayments.Allfundsmustbe
paid directly from the customer’s own official bank account to the company’s designated
account, except in special circumstances with justifications. Accepting an unauthorized
third-party payment will result in disciplinary action, ranging from internal warnings and
financial penalties to termination. The responsible employee and their manager will be held
liable for any financial or legal losses incurred by us.
 Our finance department is required to verify the application and documents required for an
exception. The customer must submit a formal application via an official letter, stating the
reason for entrusting a third party to make the payment, the name of the third-party payer, and
– 176 –

=== PAGE 185 ===
BUSINESS
the nature of their relationship or entrustment. The chief executive officer has to approve any
transaction over RMB1.0 million, and chief financial officer has to approve any transaction
belowthisamount.Theofficialapprovalmustbesubmittedandobtainedthroughourcompany
system.
 To prevent fraud or money laundering activities and ensure the accuracy and completeness of
ouraccountingbooksandrecords,wefurtherstrengthenedourknow-your-customerprocedures
to gain a comprehensive understanding of our customers and performing verification of
payment details against our records to confirm payments are made in accordance with the
agreements. If any abnormalities are detected, we will promptly liaise with such customers for
verification and correction. In addition, our sales team will hold regular meetings with
customers to gain insights into their business operations, thereby reducing the risk of
involvement in fraudulent or money laundering activities.
Based on the follow-up review of the implementation of these measures, our Directors are of the
view that these measures are effective and adequate in preventing unauthorized Third-Party Payment
Arrangements and the associated risks. Going forward, our Directors will continue to oversee the
effectiveness of the aforementioned enhanced internal control measures on the Third-Party Payment
Arrangements. Based on documents and information provided by the Company and the independent due
diligence work conducted by the Joint Sponsors, nothing has come to the Joint Sponsors’ attention that
would cause them to disagree with our Directors’ view.
DATA SECURITY AND PRIVACY
Inthecourseofourbusiness,wecollect,storeandprocessbusinessdataandtransactiondata.During
the use of our robotic products, we do not collect any personal data or information from customers. Our

TRADE RESTRICTIONS, SANCTIONS, AND TARIFF
U.S. Export Control Implications
The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (the “BIS”) maintains various
lists of entities and individuals subject to enhanced export controls.Among these, the Entity List imposes
trade restrictions on designated foreign persons, including companies, research institutions, government
and private organizations, and individuals. Listed parties are assigned specific licensing requirements on
the basis of the national security and/or foreign policy considerations associated with the entity’s
designation on the Entity List, and restricted from accessing certain U.S.-origin items, such as goods,
software, and technology. Certain entities on the Entity List also carry a footnote 4 designation. For these
entities, “items subject to the EAR” includes not only U.S.-origin items but also foreign-produced items
that fall under EAR pursuant to Part 734.9(e)(2), such as products derived from specified U.S. technology
or equipment.
Certain customers of ours have been listed on the Entity List (the “Entity List Customers”), and
within them, several have been designated with Footnote 4 (the “Footnote 4 Entity List Customers”).
During the Track Record Period, we had transactions with 17 Entity List Customers, and the revenue
generated from Entity List Customers accounted for approximately 2.8%, 0.4% and 1.7% of our total
revenue for 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. Within the Entity List Customers, we had transactions
with five Footnote 4 Entity List Customers during the Track Record Period, and the revenue generated
from them accounted for approximately 0.4%, 0.1% and 0.2% of our total revenue in 2023, 2024, and
2025, respectively. Nonetheless, our International Sanctions LegalAdvisor is of the view that transactions
with the Entity List Customers and Footnote 4 Entity List Customers would not be subject to the EAR on

The U.S. Outbound Investment Rules
The U.S. outbound investment review mechanism in force is narrowly targeted at certain types of
investments in the country and typically the restrictions target sensitive technologies and products critical
for military, intelligence, mass-surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities. If no covered activity is
involved in the transaction, the transaction is not within the jurisdictional scope of the U.S. outbound
investment review.
We have developed our embodied AI model training platform, which is a system that spans from
basic automation to artificial general intelligence. We are advised by our International Sanctions Legal
Advisor that our business should be categorized as a notifiable activity, as developing an AI system
intended to be used for the control of robotics systems. Therefore, we are advised by our International
Sanctions LegalAdvisor that we are a “covered foreign person” under the Outbound Investment Rule and
the Global Offering may constitute a notifiable transaction under the relevant rules, and U.S persons
participating in the Global Offering may be subject to notification obligations to the U.S. Treasury, while
subsequent secondary market transactions are generally exempted. Once our H Shares are issued and
become publicly traded, subsequent purchasers are exempted under the publicly traded securities
exception. Investors that are U.S. persons should consult their own legal counsel regarding the applicable
compliance requirements, including their notification obligation, if any, under the Outbound Investment
Rule in connection with the Global Offering. See “Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our General
Operations and Industry—We are exposed to risks associated with U.S. Executive Order 14105 and its
implementing regulations that prohibit and require notification by U.S. persons for certain investments.”
Tariff
OurDirectorsareoftheviewthatthetariffmeasuresacrosstheU.S.,theEuropeanUnionandChina
do not have a material adverse impact on our business operations and financial condition, primarily
because (1) our business operates through localized manufacturing and production activities in China,
which are insulated from tariff-related cost pressures; (2) we had limited revenue generated from overseas

cross-border exposure as most of our suppliers are China-based suppliers such that we do not rely on
overseas supply chains.
Additionally, our Directors are of the view that we have no material indirect exposure arising from
the tariff measures across the U.S., the European Union and China, primarily because (1) over 90% of our
revenue in 2025 was generated from direct sales to end customers located in Chinese Mainland, including
manufacturers and system integrators which incorporate our products in their production process in
Chinese Mainland, where such transactions do not involve cross-border tariff exposure, and we generally
do not engage in direct exports to the United States nor in re-export arrangements involving the United
States market, and (2) approximately 99% of our overseas revenue are conducted under trade terms where
customers bear the responsibility for transportation, customs clearance and applicable tariffs and duties,
including commonly used Incoterms such as EXW (Ex Works) or FOB (Free on Board) and other similar
arrangements, with only approximately 1% of our export transactions conducted under DDP (Delivered
Duty Paid) terms, under which we are responsible for tariffs and duties.

ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIALAND GOVERNANCE
We believe the effective management of environmental, social and corporate governance (“ESG”)
matters is important to our long-term success. We are committed to promoting long-term growth in a
prudent and responsible manner, and regard ESG as an integral component of both value creation and risk
management.
ESG Governance
We have established a systematic ESG governance framework to ensure that ESG considerations are
effectively integrated into our strategy, risk management and operations. Our Board assumes ultimate
oversight of ESG matters, regularly reviews material issues, assesses potential business and financial
impacts and guides risk response measures. Our Board also conducts regular reviews of ESG-related risks
and opportunities and provides guidance on the formulation of corresponding response measures. Our
Board oversees areas such as ethics, environmental compliance, supply chain management and employee
development, ensuring that related risks and opportunities are addressed effectively. Regular ESG
reporting and training are arranged to help our Board stay informed of emerging risks, regulatory changes
and global sustainability trends.
We have also established internal control mechanisms covering ESG policy implementation, target
progression, disclosure and performance evaluation, and we continue to refine governance arrangements
with business development and regulatory requirements. We will further enhance our Board and
management oversight of ESG matters and refine governance and execution processes to strengthen
overall sustainability management.
Our production processes mainly consist of robot assembly, testing and R&D, and we do not fall
within high-pollution or high-energy-consumption industries. Our overall ESG risk exposure is relatively
low. With reference to publicly available disclosures of listed comparable companies in the robotics
industry, our environmental emission and resource consumption intensity indicators are within the
reasonable range of the industry. As our business further matures and ESG data accumulation advances,
we will continue to conduct industry benchmarking and supplement comparable quantitative information
in due course.

=== PAGE 192 ===
BUSINESS
ESG Materiality Assessment
We are actively developing a well-structured and closed-loop ESG management system. At the
governance mechanism level, the Board will take the lead in conducting materiality assessments of ESG
issues, positioning this as a core component of sustainable development. The Board will oversee the
reviewprocessforESGrisktopicsthatimpactbusinessoperations,whilealsotrackingtheimplementation
of related management measures throughout their lifecycle. This ensures that ESG management advances
in step with corporate strategy.
Within the topic assessment process, we are committed to establishing a full-cycle assessment
mechanism for ESG material issues. This involves first conducting a comprehensive review of potential
risks and opportunities related to our business, taking into account internal and external factors, short- to
medium-term strategic plans, and financial implications, to compile a list of material topics. We will then
engage in regular communication with key stakeholders, encouraging their participation in ESG surveys
to fully incorporate their feedback. Finally, using stakeholder input as a key reference and integrating
conclusions from management evaluations, we will confirm and prioritize material issues, forming the
annual ESG materiality assessment results.
At the indicator management level, based on the annual ESG materiality assessment outcomes, we
will establish quantifiable key performance indicators for core material topics. By closely monitoring
these indicators, we aim to achieve dynamic monitoring and control of risk exposures associated with
relevant topics, as well as ongoing tracking of performance. This approach enhances the scientific rigor
and traceability of our ESG management.
ESG Risks and Opportunities
The Board will continuously monitor environmental, social, and governance risks that may impact
the business, strategy, and finances, and will, under its supervision, persistently identify and monitor
short-, medium-, and long-term ESG risks and opportunities. Within a reasonable range of assumptions
and in line with actual production operations and the Company’s strategic development, specific
quantifiable ESG risk indicators will be established.
We will set climate risk assumptions against the backdrop of the ongoing advancement of global and
China’s“dualcarbon”policies,thegradualrefinementandabsenceofdisruptiveadjustmentstoregulatory
standards related to new energy and low-carbon manufacturing, and the continuity of industry standards
such as ESG disclosure and carbon footprint accounting. Targets will be established, such as the increase
in the renewable energy usage rate and the attainment rate for R&D investment in low-carbon

emphasisandexecutioncapabilitiesamongupstreamanddownstreamsuppliers,theirabilitytocollaborate

Environmental Protection
We place a strong emphasis on environmental protection and have taken proactive measures to
control the negative environmental impact of our business. Our business operations, including the
manufacturing process of our robots, may generate solid waste and hazardous waste. We adopt advanced
environmentally friendly manufacturing equipment, install environmental protection facilities for the
treatment of exhaust gases and regular testing, and optimize our manufacturing process to reduce the
generation of pollutants and other negative impacts during the manufacturing process.
Based on the technical characteristics of the robotics manufacturing industry and key environmental
risk concerns, we have formulated targeted and innovative environmental ESG policies and measures,
establishing a closed-loop system, particularly in full life-cycle material management and standardized
waste disposal.We explicitly integrate environmental risk control into the entire process of product R&D,
manufacturing, and waste disposal, clearly refraining from using highly polluting raw materials, adopting
high-emission production processes, or disposing of any waste in violation of regulations, thereby
ensuring full compliance with the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Prevention and Control
of Environmental Pollution by Solid Waste and other domestic and international standards. We focus on
breakthroughs in areas such as the application of lightweight materials, optimization of low-emission
processes, and waste recycling technologies, leveraging core robotics technologies to contribute to
environmental governance and achieve “pollution control through technology.”
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not been subject to
any administrative penalties by the competent environmental protection authorities for violations of PRC
environmental laws, and our PRC LegalAdvisor is of the view that we have complied with the applicable
PRC laws and regulations regarding environmental protection in all material respects.

Waste Management
We implement a refined system for waste classification, storage, and disposal management:
For general solid waste, packaging materials, plastic scraps, metal waste, and similar items are
categorized in detail. Recyclable materials such as aluminum scraps and plastic shell waste are regularly
collected by the administrative department and sold to professional renewable resource enterprises to
achieve material recycling. Non-recyclable materials are transferred to the plant management department
for centralized and harmless treatment.

Workplace and Occupational Safety
We have established workplace safety policies and procedures to ensure that all parts of our
operations are compliant with applicable laws and regulations in all material respects. Specifically, we
established safety inspection team to execute and implement our workplace safety policies. Our safety
inspection team is responsible for identifying potential safety risks and devising corresponding treatment,
including those relating to electrical devices, manufacturing equipment, hazardous materials and building
structures. Upon identifying any such safety hazards, our safety inspection team maintains written records
of hazard description and underlying causes and reports to our safety manager, and collaborates with
operational departments to complete corrective actions based on the identified hazards. In addition, we
adoptedaseriesofpreventivemeasurestofurtherensureworkplaceandoccupationalsafety.Forinstance,

Supply Chain Management
We are committed to establishing a responsible supply chain system, ensuring that suppliers comply

safety, and business ethics. We implement ESG due diligence on suppliers through a combination of
document reviews and on-site audits. In terms of environmental management, we review suppliers’

governance, the emphasis is on reviewing suppliers’ business ethics standards and anti-corruption

PATH TO PROFITABILITY
Our business model adopts a long-term, investment-led approach and focuses on value creation
through sustained investment in core technology platforms upfront, including the development of our
self-developed software algorithms, such as the xCore control system, which form the backbone of our
technological foundation and validation platform and enable new functions and performance
enhancements to be deployed across multiple product generations. As such, we recorded adjusted net
losses (non-HKFRS measure) of RMB101.3 million, RMB72.5 million and RMB41.7 million in 2023,
2024 and 2025, respectively, primarily as a result of continued R&D investment and the expansion of our
sales and marketing efforts, with R&D expenses of RMB59.4 million, RMB54.2 million and RMB65.5
million and selling and marketing expenses of RMB54.9 million, RMB63.0 million and RMB75.6 million
during the same periods, respectively, which we believe are necessary to support our technology
development and business growth and have contributed to the observed but progressively narrowing
losses. We have historically achieved continuous revenue growth as we successfully developed and
launched new products and solutions during theTrack Record Period. Our proactive endeavors in product
commercialization and market expansion have contributed to our revenue growth during theTrack Record
Period.OurrevenuewasRMB267.0million,RMB325.3millionandRMB521.7millionin2023,2024and
2025, respectively. We are one of the earliest domestic companies in China capable of producing both
industrial and collaborative robots at an annual production exceeding 1,000 units, reflecting an industry

industrial robots ranked No. 6 among domestic providers in the Chinese market in 2025, with a market

countries and regions.
WehavecontinuouslyincreasedinvestmentinR&Dforfurthertechnologicalupgradesanditerations
of our robotics products and solutions. With our forward design, modularly designed hardware and

During the Track Record Period, while our revenue grew rapidly, our overall revenue scale was still
insufficient to fully absorb our largely fixed cost base, resulting in limited operating leverage. Our
business model focuses on long-term value creation through sustained investment in core technology
platforms, including internally developed software algorithms, such as the xCore control system, and
hardware components, such as self-developed servos, controllers, torque sensors and motors. Under this
model, a minimum level of R&D capability, engineering personnel and operating infrastructure must be
maintained irrespective of short-term revenue fluctuations. As a result, our operating expenses did not
increase in direct proportion to revenue during the early stage of revenue scaling. In particular, we
continued to make significant investments in R&D to strengthen our technology leadership, expand our
productportfolioandsupportlong-termgrowth.Allofourroboticproductsaredevelopedunderaforward
design and validation framework and based on our proprietary xCore control system, which allows new

and 12.6% of our total revenue in the same years, respectively.As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025,
we employed 92, 105 and 157 R&D personnel, respectively, representing 22.8%, 22.2% and 25.5% of our
total workforce, with the relevant employee benefit expenses accounting for 69.0%, 72.7% and 73.7% of
our research and development expenses in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. These investments
supported continuous product iteration, expansion of product categories and forward-looking R&D
initiatives, including embodied intelligence products, which are expected to contribute to future revenue
growth but had not yet fully translated into profitability during the Track Record Period.
In parallel, we invested heavily in building an increasingly larger sales and marketing team to
support business expansion and customer acquisition. Our selling and marketing expenses were RMB54.9
million, RMB63.0 million and RMB75.6 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, representing
20.6%, 19.4% and 14.6% of our total revenue of the same years, respectively. These expenses were

While these investments adversely affected short-term profitability, they laid the foundation for future
revenue growth. The declining selling and marketing expense ratio during the Track Record Period
demonstrates emerging economies of scale. As our revenue continues to scale up, we expect to achieve
economies of scale with enhanced operating leverage, whereby operating expenses would not increase
proportionally with revenue. Together with the derecognition of redemption liabilities following the
termination of redemption rights related to the Pre-IPO Investments upon the Listing, and the gradual
realization of benefits from our prior R&D and sales and marketing investments, we believe we are well
positioned to achieve profitability in the future.
Furthermore, revenue generation for our different product categories commenced at different stages,
with industrial robots and robotic solutions beginning in 2017, collaborative robots in 2020 and embodied
intelligent robots in 2021. Such staggered commercialization reflects the evolving nature of our product
portfolio and contributes to a gradual build-up of revenue streams rather than a one-off step change in
revenue scale. In addition, continuous expansion in our robot models and categories required additional
time for product adaptation and customer qualification. We provide industrial robots spanning ten series
and 27 models, collaborative robots comprising three series and 15 models, and have also launched six

Driving Our Revenue Growth
Rapid growth of industrial robot markets
We believe that we are well-positioned to further unleash the commercialization potential of our
major product lines and monetize from the market tailwinds of embodied intelligent robots in particular.
According to the CIC Report, China’s industrial robot market size is expected to grow from RMB23.9
billion in 2025 to RMB37.3 billion in 2030, at a CAGR of 9.3%. We expect to take advantage of the
significantupsidepotentialoftheChinesemarket.Underpinnedbyourhomegrownadvantages,weexpect
to leverage the unique benefits of our products and solutions, our solid relationship with downstream
customers and our elevating market recognition to capitalize from the Chinese and overseas markets.
Due to our early-mover advantage, the competitiveness and innovativeness of our product portfolio,
our robust technology foundation and strong relationship with our customers, we achieved significant
growth during the Track Record Period. Our total revenue increased from RMB267.0 million for 2023 to
RMB325.3 million for 2024, and further to RMB521.7 million for 2025, at a CAGR of 39.8% over the
same years. In terms of revenue in 2025, we ranked No. 6 among domestic robot providers in China’s
industrialrobotmarketwithamarketshareof0.9%,andNo.6inChina’scollaborativerobotmarket,with
amarketshareof4.8%accordingtotheCICReport.Wearealsotheonlyproviderofflexiblecollaborative
robots at an annual production exceeding 1,000 units among the top six collaborative robot providers in
China. We are also one of the top five providers in China’s embodied intelligent robotic arm market with
a market share of 6.3%, according to the same source.
Our strategy to capture market growth focuses on scaling up validated products in mainstream
application industries. For instance, we have developed 37 new robotic product series during the Track
Record Period, with a particular advantage in light payload industrial robots. In industries such as
automotive and 3C electronics, we have achieved large scale commercial deployment with well known
customers.See“—OurCompetitiveStrengths—EstablishedCustomerandPartnershipNetworkBackedby
Our Service Capability and Modular Plug-ins and Open Interfaces.” With core technologies and product
performance already validated by marquee customers, our industrial robot business has entered a
replication stage, where existing customers typically place bulk repeat orders upon capacity expansion,
and other customers within the same industry are willing to directly procure in volume by referencing
these proven application cases. We believe this enables our industrial robot revenue to grow at a rate
higher than the industry average.

Technological innovation and product iteration
Leveraging the success of our offerings, we continue to iterate and expand our robotic portfolio to
improve their adaptability, accuracy and efficiency, thereby strengthening our competitive advantages and
enhancing our market presence. For example, we plan to enhance our robot body design and develop
embodied intelligence and perceptual interaction, which will serve to advance our robots from mere
execution tools to true intelligent partners.
We plan to increase investment in core robotic technologies to strengthen our competitive barriers
and enhance product capabilities. The xCore control system serves as the technological backbone across
our product portfolio, integrating motion control, force control, safety management and real-time
operation. This unified control architecture allows new functions and performance enhancements to be
rolled out across multiple product generations, enabling us to capture the commercial value of ongoing
technological upgrades through successive product iterations, rather than relying on one-off sales. Our
focus will include advancing high-precision, high-speed control systems, integrated drive and control
modules, and electronic control architectures.
We will also enhance our robot body design and validation platform, and further expand in-house
R&D of core components, primarily including specialized servos, safety controllers, and encoders.Across
all product offerings, we adopt a structured lifecycle comprising technology and platform pre-research,
product design and development, testing and validation, pilot production, batch order delivery and
subsequent iteration or replacement. This standardized pipeline enables us to efficiently translate
platform-level technological advances into commercially deployable products, while maintaining high
performance, stability and reliability required for large-scale industrial applications. See “—Our Robotics
Offerings—Our Product Development Lifecycle and Business Process—Product Development Lifecycle.”
For motors and torque sensors, we will adopt an independent design and OEM production model to meet
the demanding requirements of certain high-end application scenarios.
To expand our business scale, we continue to enrich and expand our offerings to meet the increasing
demand of the rapidly evolving market. Our strategy involves developing new products that cater to the
dynamic needs of the market, thereby enhancing our market share and visibility. Leveraging our R&D
team consisting of industry experts and engineers with experience in the robotics industry, we intend to
focus on improvements in product performance, durability and usability. This includes continuous
development of process packages for specific applications, which simplifies product use in targeted
applicationsandopensupnewmarkets.Inembodiedintelligence,weplantodevelopanditerateproducts,
primarily including humanoid arms and full humanoid robots. We will open our hardware design, mass
production capabilities, and robot control platform to partners.We expect these efforts to drive significant
growth and position us at the forefront of the industry. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we have

Improving our Net Profit Margin
Continually improving our net profit margin is crucial to achieving long-term profitability. From a
revenue structure perspective, we expect our overall gross profit margin to improve as the contribution
fromhigher-marginproductsandoverseasmarketsincreases.Inparticular,embodiedintelligentrobotsare
expected to carry higher gross profit margins compared to our traditional product offerings. As revenue
from such products increases, their higher margin profile is expected to structurally improve our overall
gross profit margin. In parallel, our overseas business, which accounted for less than 10% of our total
revenue in 2025, is expected to expand going forward. We will accelerate our overseas expansion by
deepening market penetration through localized operations and targeted marketing. Our strategy includes
introducing our robotic products and replicating mature domestic robotic solutions to overseas markets,
aswellasestablishinglocalsalesandservicecentersinkeyregionssuchasEurope,SoutheastAsia,Japan,
andSouthKorea.Theseteamswillbestaffedwithlanguage-proficientandindustry-experiencedpersonnel
to deliver regionally adapted products and customized solutions that meet local testing and certification
standards, such as the CE certification for EU, the UL standard for NorthAmerica, and the KC standards
for South Korea. We will also focus on engaging high-end overseas customers and securing partnerships
with overseas industry leaders. During the Track Record Period and as of the Latest Practicable Date, we
had secured confirmed orders for over 1,400 robots from overseas customers, with over 1,300 robots
additional indicative demands from overseas supported by letters of intention. Overseas projects are
typically more application-driven, which generally involve higher service and solution content and
thereforeprovidegreaterflexibilityinpricing,whichwebelievewillfurthersupportmarginimprovement.
This expansion is supported by established application cases with well-known customers in Europe,Asia
and NorthAmerica, which provide local reference points and facilitate replication without a proportional
increase in fixed costs.

continues to grow.This will be further bolstered by the ongoing ramp-up of our production base in Jining,
Shandong Province. We plan to introduce more automated production equipment and processes to boost
production efficiency and capacity, further reducing the manufacturing costs for our robots. We will also

Wealsoaimtostreamlineoursupplychainmanagementandmaintaincontroloverrawmaterialcosts

of 2026 compared to December 2025, while extending payment terms to 90 days. Furthermore, we have
entered into stock preparation agreements and implemented vendor-managed inventory consignment
models with core suppliers. These arrangements allow us to reduce inventory levels, improve inventory
turnover and lower capital tied up in working capital, thereby supporting both gross margin stability and
net operating cash flow improvement. As we continue to enhance automation and intelligence in our
roboticproductionprocessthroughthedevelopmentofautomatedunitstationsforassembly,handling,and
other tasks, we can further enhance our production efficiency, product quality, and cost-effectiveness.As
a result of these measures, we expect unit production costs to decrease in the future.
We plan to further increase operational efficiency to improve net profit margin. We will enhance
customer acquisition efficiency, primarily driven by (1) brand and product loyalty for our direct sales
channelsanddistributorship;(2)achievinggreatercostefficiencywithoursalesandmarketinginitiatives;
and (3) the advancement of new functions within our existing series to further enhance marketing
efficiency with more targeted applications. Specifically, our established application cases featuring
industry-leadingcustomersbothdomesticallyandinternationallyserveaseffectiveendorsements,thereby
shortening sales cycles and reducing customer validation costs. In addition, we are enhancing the use of
customer relationship management systems to better manage sales leads, customer engagement, and order
conversion. In overseas markets, we leverage local reference projects and sales networks to achieve
revenue growth without a proportional increase in fixed costs. We will also benefit from enhanced
economies of scale, as we keep our general and administrative expenses relatively stable in relation to our
revenue. This stability will contribute to a stronger financial position, ultimately supporting our path to
profitability.
In terms of R&D efficiency, we adopt a standardized, platform-based product development
framework anchored by our proprietary xCore control system and forward design and validation
framework. This approach allows us to reuse core technologies, algorithms and modules across multiple
product generations, reducing marginal R&D costs and shortening development cycles for new or
derivative products. Importantly, our R&D efforts also focus on cost-oriented engineering, whereby
technological advancement directly contributes to unit cost reduction. For example, we have self-
developed high-voltage servos for industrial robots, which reduce unit costs by over 15% compared to
externallyprocuredalternatives.Inaddition,newerversionsofourrobotsincreasinglyadoptdomestically
sourced low-voltage servo components, reducing unit costs by over 20% compared to previous versions.
These R&D-driven cost reduction measures allow us to improve product cost competitiveness and gross
margin while maintaining performance and reliability, with benefits that scale directly with shipment
volume.
Improving Net Operating Cash Outflow Position
We plan to improve our net operating cash outflow position through four initiatives, including (1)
optimizing payment terms in sales contracts; (2) further strengthening our tiered aging alert mechanism
for trade receivables, coupled with rigorous monitoring of overdue payments; and (3) extending supplier
payment terms through the use of instruments such as acceptances and letters of credit to ease cash flow
pressure. This coordinated approach of accelerating receivables while optimizing payables is designed to
shorten our net operating cycle, enhance liquidity security, and reinforce financial stability.
IMPACT OF COVID-19 PANDEMIC
The COVID-19 pandemic, which began in 2020 and lasted for over three years, had a notable
influence on global industries. Overall, our Directors are of the view that the COVID-19 pandemic had no
material adverse impact on our business operations and financial performance during the Track Record
Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, particularly in light of the significant revenue growth
achieved following the pandemic, driven by our launch of numerous new robotic product series, as well
as the commencement of new collaborations with business partners.

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
Our Directors recognize the importance of good corporate governance in management and internal
procedures so as to achieve effective accountability. Save as disclosed below, our Group is expected to
comply with the code provisions of the Corporate Governance Code as set out in Appendix C1 to the
Listing Rules.
Pursuant to code provision C.2.1 of Part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code, companies listed on
the Stock Exchange are expected to comply with, but may choose to deviate from the requirement that the
roles of chairman and chief executive should be separate and should not be performed by the same
individual. We do not have a separate chairman and chief executive and Mr. Tuo currently performs these
two roles. Our Board believes that vesting the roles of both the chairman of our Board and the general
manager of our Company in the same person has the benefit of (1) ensuring consistent leadership within
our Company, (2) enabling more effective and efficient overall strategic planning for our Company, and
(3) facilitating the flow of information between the management and our Board. Our Board considers that
thebalanceofpowerandauthorityforthepresentarrangementwillnotbeimpairedandthisstructurewill
enable our Company to make and implement decisions promptly and effectively. Our Board will continue
to review and consider splitting the roles of the chairman of our Board and the president of our Company
at a time when it is appropriate by taking into account the circumstances of our Company as a whole.
COMPENSATION OF DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT
The compensation and remuneration of the Directors and members of the senior management of our
Company are determined by the Shareholders’meetings and the Board of Directors as appropriate in the
form of salaries and bonuses. The Company also reimburses them for expenses which are necessary and
reasonably incurred in providing services to the Company or discharging their duties in relation to the
operations of the Company. When reviewing and determining the specific remuneration packages for our
Directors and members of the senior management of the Company, the Shareholders’ meetings and the
Board of Directors take into account factors such as salaries paid by comparable companies, time
commitment, level of responsibilities, employment elsewhere in our Group and desirability of
performance-basedremuneration.AsrequiredbytherelevantPRClawsandregulations,theCompanyalso
participates in various defined contribution plans organized by relevant provincial and municipal
government authorities and welfare schemes for employees of the Company, including medical insurance,
injury insurance, unemployment insurance, pension insurance, maternity insurance and housing provident
fund.
The Company offers executive Directors and senior management members, who are our employees,
compensation in the form of salaries, bonuses, social security plans, housing provident fund plans and
other benefits. The independent non-executive Directors receive compensation based on their
responsibilities.

CONVERSION OF OUR UNLISTED SHARES INTO H SHARES
Pursuant to the regulations prescribed by the securities regulatory authorities of the State Council
and the Articles of Association, the Unlisted Shares may be converted into overseas-listed Shares. Such
converted Shares could be listed or traded on an overseas stock exchange, provided that prior to the
conversion and trading of such converted Shares, any requisite internal approval process has been duly
completed, all the filling procedures with relevant PRC regulatory authorities, including the CSRC are
followed. In addition, such conversion and trading shall comply with the regulations, requirements and
procedures prescribed by the relevant overseas stock exchange. If any of the Unlisted Shares are to be
converted, listed and traded as H Shares on the Stock Exchange, such conversion, listing and trading will
need to be filed with relevant PRC regulatory authorities, including the CSRC, and the approval of the
Stock Exchange.
Filing with the CSRC
According to the Trial Administrative Measures of Overseas Securities Offering and Listing by
Domestic Companies (境內企業境外發行證券和上市管理試行辦法) announced by the CSRC, for an
H-share listed company, shareholders of its domestic unlisted shares applying to convert such shares into
shares listed and traded on an overseas trading venue shall conform to relevant regulations promulgated
by the CSRC, and authorize the domestic company to file with the CSRC on their behalf.
In accordance with the Guidelines for the “Full Circulation” Program for Domestic Unlisted Shares
of H-share Listed Companies (H股公司境內未上市股份申請“全流通”業務指引) announced by the CSRC,
an unlisted domestic joint stock company may apply for “full circulation” when applying for an overseas
initial public offering.

OVERVIEW
We primarily manufacture and sell robotic products, and, to a lesser extent, provide related robotic
solutionsinChineseMainlandandoverseasmarkets,dedicatedtothedesign,development,manufacturing
and commercialization of our offerings. Leveraging our proprietary technology platform, we have
cultivated a dynamic robotic application portfolio, comprising industrial robots, flexible collaborative
robots, embodied intelligent robots, and related robotic solutions characterized by performance, agility,
intelligence, safety and robustness.
We achieved robust growth and continually improved gross profit margin during the Track Record
Period.OurrevenuewasRMB267.0million,RMB325.3millionandRMB521.7millionin2023,2024and
2025, respectively. We recorded gross profit of RMB30.6 million, RMB71.2 million and RMB114.2
million, respectively, representing gross profit margin of 11.4%, 21.9% and 21.9%, respectively. We
recorded loss for the year of RMB157.5 million, RMB191.8 million and RMB179.3 million in the same
periods, respectively. We recorded adjusted net loss for the year (non-HKFRS measure) of RMB101.3
million, RMB72.5 million and RMB41.7 million in the same periods, respectively.
KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our business, results of operations and financial condition are affected by the general factors
influencing the sectors that we operate in. For instance, as we operate in the rapidly growing robotics
market, our business, financial performance, results of operations and future growth are affected by the
development of the global robotics industry, especially the industrial robot industry and the growth of the
industries in which our customers operate.
Chinese industrial robot market players are accelerating global expansion and breaking through
growth bottlenecks through continuous technological upgrades. Driven by increasing domestic
substitution, domestic players have significantly enhanced their core technologies, product performance,
and system integration capabilities, gradually building the competitiveness to rival global leaders.
Meanwhile, breakthroughs in high-speed, high-precision motion control and core components have
enabled domestic players to challenge foreign dominance in the high-end segment, creating substantial
opportunities for China’s industrial robot industry to establish a new global growth paradigm.According
to the CIC Report, the sales volume of robotic products in China’s industrial robot industry is expected
to increase from 293.9 thousands in 2025 to 465.3 thousands in 2030, at a CAGR of 9.6%. We expect to
continue to leverage from the market opportunities to drive our sales and revenue growth in the future. In
particular, we expect that our embodied intelligent robots will be one of our next growth engines.
According to the CIC Report, China’s embodied intelligent robot market is in a stage of rapid growth,
whichisexpectedtoreachapproximatelyRMB460.0billionby2035.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,we
